definition_zh: 藻类的；由藻类组成的；藻类造成的
definition_en: relating to, consisting of, or caused by algae
core_image: 浅水池壁上那层滑腻的绿膜，肉眼只看到一片绿色，显微镜下才是一团单细胞生物
scene: 池塘边，几个孩子发现浅水处的石头上覆着一层滑腻的绿膜，老师蹲下来指着水样说，那是微型藻类在迅速繁殖。 A thick algal film had formed on the stones where the water was warm and still.
sceneCN: 这里 algal 指「藻类形成的、藻类的」（第 1 个义项：与藻类相关或由藻类构成）；句意为在温暖静止的浅水处，石头上已经结了一层厚厚的藻膜。

pos.zh: 藻类的；由藻类组成的；由藻类引起的

derivatives.zh: 藻类（alga 的复数，也作集合名）

senses.title: Relating to algae as organisms
senses.titleCN: 与藻类这一生物类群有关
senses.definition: relating to algae, the simple photosynthetic organisms that live in water and damp places
senses.definitionCN: 与藻类有关的；藻类指生活在水中或潮湿处、能进行光合作用的简单生物
senses.example: Algal cells were counted under the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 藻细胞在显微镜下被逐一计数。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun alga into an adjective of relation, so algal means 'of algae' before it means anything more specific.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词 alga 变成表关系的形容词，因此 algal 的基础义就是「藻的」，其余义项都由此细化。

senses.title: Consisting of a mass of algae
senses.definition: made up of a dense layer or mass of algae
senses.definitionCN: 由密集的藻类层或藻类群体构成的
senses.example: A green algal mat covered the rock at the outflow.
senses.exampleCN: 出水口的岩石上覆着一层绿色的藻席。
senses.why: Because algae often grow as a sheet rather than as separate plants, the adjective came to describe the whole mat, not just its members.
senses.whyCN: 藻类常成片生长而非一株株分立，因此这个形容词也用来描述整片藻席，而不只是其中的个体。

senses.title: Caused by algae
senses.definition: brought about by the growth of algae, especially in water
senses.definitionCN: 由藻类生长所引起，尤指水体中的现象
senses.example: The reservoir turned green during an algal bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 藻华期间水库变成了绿色。
senses.why: Once algae are the cause rather than the subject, the adjective marks origin: the bloom is not algae itself but what their growth produces.
senses.whyCN: 当藻类成为原因而不是主体时，这个形容词标记来源：藻华不是藻本身，而是藻类生长造成的现象。

senses.title: Carrying algal toxins
senses.titleCN: 含藻毒素的；有毒藻产生的
senses.definition: produced by toxic algae and able to harm people or animals that drink the water
senses.definitionCN: 由有毒藻类产生、能危害饮水者或动物的
senses.example: Algal toxins forced the town to switch to bottled water.
senses.exampleCN: 藻毒素迫使全镇改用瓶装水。
senses.why: Public-health writing needed a short label for poisons made by algae, and algal toxin became that fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生写作需要一个简短标签来指藻类产生的毒素，algal toxin 于是成为固定说法。

senses.title: Used as a feedstock
senses.definition: grown or harvested as raw material for fuel, feed or chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 作为燃料、饲料或化工原料而养殖或采收的
senses.example: Algal oil is pressed from tanks of cultivated microalgae.
senses.exampleCN: 藻油由培养微藻的槽罐中压榨而来。
senses.why: Industry extended 'of algae' to 'derived from algae', because the material, not the organism, is what the refinery handles.
senses.whyCN: 工业把「藻的」扩展为「从藻得到的」，因为工厂处理的是材料而不是生物体。

senses.title: Living inside a host
senses.definition: describing algae that live within the tissue of a host organism such as a coral
senses.definitionCN: 描述生活在珊瑚等宿主体内的藻类
senses.example: Reef-building corals depend on their algal partners for sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 造礁珊瑚依赖体内的共生藻提供糖分。
senses.why: In symbiosis the algae are no longer free-living, so the adjective signals the partner role rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 在共生关系中藻类不再自由生活，因此这个形容词标示的是「伙伴角色」而非地点。

senses.title: Preserved in rock
senses.titleCN: 保存在岩层中的藻类遗迹
senses.definition: referring to structures in sedimentary rock that were built by algae
senses.definitionCN: 指沉积岩中由藻类建造的结构
senses.example: Algal limestone records shallow seas of the distant past.
senses.exampleCN: 藻灰岩记录了远古的浅海。
senses.why: Geology keeps the same adjective because the rock is still, literally, made of algal remains.
senses.whyCN: 地质学沿用同一形容词，因为这种岩石确实由藻类遗骸构成。

senses.title: Tasting or smelling of algae
senses.definition: having the earthy, fishy taste or smell associated with algae in water
senses.definitionCN: 带有水中藻类那种土腥、鱼腥的味道或气味
senses.example: The tap water had an algal taste after the warm spell.
senses.exampleCN: 回暖之后，自来水带上了藻味。
senses.why: Water-quality reports speak of algal taste and odour, so the adjective also names a sensory impression rather than an organism.
senses.whyCN: 水质报告常说「藻味与藻腥气」，于是这个形容词也指一种感官印象，而非生物体。

intro.en: Algal is an English adjective built from Latin alga 'seaweed' plus the relational suffix -al; the noun is classical, the adjective is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: algal 是英语形容词，由拉丁 alga「海藻」加表关系的后缀 -al 构成；名词是古典的，形容词是近代形成的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Alga meant 'seaweed, sea wrack'. Its deeper origin is not established; a suggested link to algere 'to be cold' is only a guess, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: alga 意为「海藻、海草」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人把它与 algere「发冷」联系起来，那只是猜测，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Classical Latin already had the adjective algosus 'full of seaweed', which shows the noun was productive long before the English form appeared.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语已有形容词 algosus「长满海藻的」，说明这个名词在英语形式出现之前早就有构词能力。

items.en: From the eighteenth century botanists used algae as a group name, and English took the Latin plural in -ae rather than adding an English -s.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，植物学家用 algae 作类群名，英语直接沿用拉丁语以 -ae 结尾的复数，而不加英语的 -s。

items.en: The adjective algal is recorded from the mid-nineteenth century, first in botanical descriptions and later in water-quality writing.
items.cn: 形容词 algal 自 19 世纪中叶有记录，最初用于植物学描述，后来进入水质研究文字。

items.en: Twentieth-century technology fixed phrases such as algal bloom, algal mat, algal toxin and algal fuel, where the adjective simply labels the source.
items.cn: 20 世纪的技术文献固定了 algal bloom、algal mat、algal toxin、algal fuel 等说法，其中形容词只标示来源。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Latin origin of alga is unsettled, and any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：alga 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，凡为它提出的印欧形式都属重构形式，而非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same word and its closest derivatives, which are constantly mixed up; group two holds adjectives from neighbouring habitats that are not interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词及其最近派生形式，最易混用；第二组是来自相邻生境的形容词，彼此不能替换。

entries.definition: One alga is a single organism; algal is the adjective made from it, never a plural.
entries.definitionCN: 一个 alga 是单个藻体；algal 是由它构成的形容词，从不用作复数。

entries.definition: The plural of alga and also the informal group name; it is a noun, so it cannot replace algal in front of another noun.
entries.definitionCN: alga 的复数，也作非正式的类群名；它是名词，不能像 algal 那样放在另一个名词前作定语。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'like', it says something looks like algae without necessarily being algal.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -oid「像」构成，表示某物看起来像藻，但不一定真的属于藻类。

entries.definition: The branch of botany that studies algae; the -logy marks a discipline, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 研究藻类的植物学分支；-logy 标示学科，而非性质。

entries.definition: Describes organisms that drift in open water, algae included; it answers where they live, while algal answers what they are.
entries.definitionCN: 描述在开阔水域漂浮生活的生物，包含藻类；它回答「住在哪里」，algal 回答「是什么」。

entries.definition: Describes life on or near the seabed; an algal mat may be benthic, but the adjective benthic says nothing about algae.
entries.definitionCN: 描述生活在海底或其附近的生物；藻席可以是底栖的，但 benthic 本身与藻类无关。

entries.definition: Covers bacteria and other single-celled organisms as well as algae, so it is broader than algal.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖细菌与其他单细胞生物，也包括藻类，因此比 algal 范围更宽。

entries.definition: Describes the process of using light to make food; many algae are photosynthetic, but the term also covers plants.
entries.definitionCN: 描述利用光能制造养分的过程；许多藻类能进行光合作用，但这个词也涵盖植物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: alga is the noun, -al makes the adjective: algal simply means 'of algae'.
normal.cn: alga 是名词，加 -al 构成形容词：algal 的意思就是「藻的」。

normal.en: The plural is algae, with Latin -ae, but algal never takes a plural ending.
normal.cn: 复数是拉丁式的 algae（-ae 结尾），但 algal 本身没有复数形式。

normal.en: Algology is the study of algae, and algologist is the person who does it.
normal.cn: algology 是藻类学，algologist 是从事藻类研究的人。

normal.en: Algicide kills algae, the way herbicide kills plants and insecticide kills insects.
normal.cn: algicide 杀藻，正如 herbicide 除草、insecticide 杀虫。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the technical senses: algal bloom, algal mat, algal toxin, algal fuel.
normal.cn: 固定搭配承担技术义：藻华、藻席、藻毒素、藻类燃料。

abstract.en: Picture a clear pond going opaque green in a single warm week.
abstract.cn: 想象一池清水在一个温暖的星期里变成不透光的绿。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of pond water holding a whole microscopic forest.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴池水里藏着一整座微观森林。

abstract.en: Picture a limestone cliff that is really a cemetery of algae turned to stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一面石灰岩崖壁，其实是被石化了的藻类墓地。

examples.en: Algal growth in the bay doubled after the fertiliser runoff.
examples.cn: 化肥径流之后，海湾里的藻类生长量翻了一倍。

examples.en: The team measured algal biomass to estimate the bloom's size.
examples.cn: 团队测量藻类生物量以估算藻华的规模。

examples.en: Coral bleached when the algal partners inside it died.
examples.cn: 当体内的共生藻死亡时，珊瑚就白化了。

dict_mnemonic.text: alga 读起来像「阿狗」——水里的藻类多得像狗毛一样糊在石头上；algal 就是「藻的」

root: 拉丁 alga「海藻」+ 英语形容词后缀 -al；alga 的更深来源不确定，与 algere「发冷」的联系只是假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all radiate from one attribute: something is of algae, made of algae, or produced by algae; the uses move from the microscope to the lake, the fuel tank, the coral polyp, the rock layer and finally the tap.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个属性展开：某物属于藻、由藻构成或由藻产生；用法从显微镜走向湖泊、燃料罐、珊瑚虫、岩层，最后走到水龙头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slippery green film on a stone, invisible cells seen as one mass.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头上那层滑腻的绿膜，看不见的细胞汇成一片。

branches.en: PLAIN ATTRIBUTE: from a microscope count to a taste in tap water, the link is simply 'of algae'.
branches.cn: 单纯属性：从显微镜计数到自来水里的味道，联系都只是「与藻有关」。

branches.en: ONE SHEET: algae grow as a mat, so the adjective names a mass rather than a specimen.
branches.cn: 成片：藻类成席生长，因此形容词指的是一片，而非一个标本。

branches.en: ALGAE AS CAUSE: a bloom and its toxins are results attributed to algae.
branches.cn: 藻为起因：藻华与其毒素都是归因于藻类的结果。

branches.en: ALGAE AS MATERIAL: industry turns the organism into oil, feed and chemicals.
branches.cn: 藻作材料：工业把生物体变成油、饲料与化工品。

branches.en: ALGAE INSIDE SOMETHING ELSE: a partner in coral tissue, a ghost in limestone.
branches.cn: 藻在别物之中：珊瑚组织里的伙伴，石灰岩里的幽灵。

intro.en: Algal can be read as a stem plus one suffix, and the stem itself supports a small family of technical words.
intro.cn: algal 可拆为一个词干加一个后缀，而这个词干本身还支撑着一小族技术词。

latinIntro.en: Latin alga 'seaweed' yields alga, algae, algal and algology in English; algosus is the classical adjective built on the same noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 alga「海藻」在英语中衍生 alga、algae、algal 与 algology；algosus 是同一名词构成的古典形容词。

items.example: The singular names one organism.
items.exampleCN: 单数形式指一个藻体。

items.meaning: algae, the group as a whole
items.example: Algae drifted in dense patches.
items.exampleCN: 藻类成片漂浮。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表关系的形容词。

items.example: An algal film covered the stones.
items.exampleCN: 一层藻膜覆盖着石头。

items.example: Algology grew out of nineteenth-century botany.
items.exampleCN: 藻类学从 19 世纪的植物学中发展出来。

items.example: The algologist sampled the kelp bed each spring.
items.exampleCN: 这位藻类学家每年春天都给海藻林取样。

items.example: The pool was treated with an algicide.
items.exampleCN: 泳池用杀藻剂处理过。

items.meaning: a gum extracted from brown algae
items.example: Alginate thickens the ice-cream mix.
items.exampleCN: 藻酸盐使冰淇淋浆料变稠。

items.meaning: a rapid overgrowth of algae in water
items.example: The algal bloom stained the shoreline green.
items.exampleCN: 藻华把岸线染成绿色。

latinEntries.structure: algosus, algosa, algosum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 海藻；海草（生长在海里的大型藻类，也指采作食物或原料的海藻）
definition_en: large algae that grow in the sea, especially when gathered as food or raw material
core_image: 退潮后的礁石上挂着一片片湿滑的褐绿色长带，随残余的水流来回摆动
scene: 退潮后，渔妇蹲在湿滑的礁石上，用镰刀割下一长条褐绿色的海藻，抖了抖水放进竹篮。 At low tide she cut a long strand of seaweed from the wet rock and shook it into her basket.
sceneCN: 这里 seaweed 指「长在海里的大型藻类，可采集的海藻」（第 2 个义项：作为采集物或食材的海藻）；句意为退潮时她从湿滑的礁石上割下一长条海藻，抖掉水放进篮子。

pos.zh: 海藻；海草（大型海生藻类）
可食用的海藻；海藻制品

derivatives.zh: 带海藻味的；长满海藻的
海藻床（成片生长的海藻区）

senses.title: Marine algae growing in the sea
senses.definition: large algae that grow attached to rocks or the seabed in salt water
senses.definitionCN: 附着在礁石或海底生长的大型海生藻类
senses.example: Seaweed covered the rocks below the tide line.
senses.exampleCN: 潮线以下的礁石上覆满了海藻。
senses.why: The compound simply says 'a weed of the sea': sea names the place, weed names a plant-like growth, and the pair covers whatever grows there in sheets.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词字面就是「海里的草」：sea 标地点，weed 标像植物的生长物，合起来泛指成片长在那里的东西。

senses.title: Seaweed gathered as food
senses.definition: seaweed harvested and prepared for eating, fresh or dried
senses.definitionCN: 采收后新鲜或干燥食用的大型海藻
senses.example: She cut a long strand of seaweed from the wet rock.
senses.exampleCN: 她从湿滑的礁石上割下一长条海藻。
senses.why: Once people gather it deliberately, the word shifts from the plant in the sea to the crop in the basket.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们有意采集，这个词就从「海里的植物」转为「篮子里的收成」。

senses.title: Raw material for industry
senses.definition: seaweed processed to extract gums, minerals or chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 经加工以提取胶质、矿物质或化学品的海藻
senses.example: Brown seaweed is processed for alginate used in food and medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 褐藻被加工成用于食品与医药的褐藻胶。
senses.why: The same harvest feeds factories, so the word also names a bulk material rather than a plant.
senses.whyCN: 同样的收成也供给工厂，因此这个词也指大宗原料，而不只是植物。

senses.title: Fertiliser spread on fields
senses.definition: seaweed used as mulch or soil improver on farmland
senses.definitionCN: 用作覆盖物或土壤改良剂的海藻
senses.example: Crofters spread seaweed on the potato beds each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 佃农每年春天把海藻铺在土豆地里。
senses.why: Coastal farming long used what the tide delivered, so seaweed became a word for free fertiliser.
senses.whyCN: 沿海农业长期利用潮水送来的东西，于是 seaweed 也成了「免费的肥料」。

senses.title: Weed cast up on the shore
senses.titleCN: 被浪冲上岸的腐烂海藻
senses.definition: seaweed washed ashore and left to rot along the high-water line
senses.definitionCN: 被冲上岸、在高潮线一带腐烂的海藻
senses.example: Flies rose from the seaweed at the high-water mark.
senses.exampleCN: 高潮线处的海藻上飞起一群苍蝇。
senses.why: Here the plant is dead and stranded; the word follows the material wherever the tide leaves it.
senses.whyCN: 此时植物已死并被搁浅，这个词跟着物质走，潮水把它留在哪里就指哪里。

senses.title: Underwater forest and habitat
senses.titleCN: 海藻林与其中的栖息地
senses.definition: a dense stand of large seaweed that shelters fish and invertebrates
senses.definitionCN: 为鱼类与无脊椎动物提供遮蔽的密集大型海藻群落
senses.example: Kelp, the tallest seaweed, forms forests along cold coasts.
senses.exampleCN: 海带是最高的海藻，在寒冷海岸形成森林。
senses.why: Ecology treats the mass as habitat, so seaweed names a place as well as a plant.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把这一大片视为栖息地，因此 seaweed 既指植物也指地点。

senses.title: A sheet used to wrap food
senses.definition: a thin dried sheet of seaweed used to wrap rice or fillings
senses.definitionCN: 用来包米饭或馅料的干燥海藻薄片
senses.example: She wrapped the rice in a sheet of seaweed.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一片海藻把米饭卷起来。
senses.why: Cuisine turns the plant into a countable sheet, and the word follows the product's new shape.
senses.whyCN: 烹饪把植物变成可数的薄片，词义随之跟到成品的新形态上。

senses.title: A tangled mass, figuratively
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：纠缠成团的一大堆
senses.definition: a dense, disordered tangle that resembles seaweed in a harbour
senses.definitionCN: 像港里海藻那样密集而杂乱的一团东西
senses.example: A seaweed of old rope and nets clogged the repair shed.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆旧绳索和渔网像海藻一样缠塞了修理棚。
senses.why: The figurative use keeps only the shape of the mass: something long, wet and hopelessly entangled.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义只保留「一团」的形态：长长的、湿的、缠得解不开。

intro.en: Seaweed is a native English compound of sea and weed, not a borrowing; its two halves are both Old English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: seaweed 是英语本族复合词，由 sea 与 weed 组成，并非外来借词；两半都来自古英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sǣ meant 'sea, lake, sheet of water' and survives in sea, as well as in compounds such as sea-bird and sea-wall.
items.cn: sǣ 意为「海、湖、大片水域」，留存为 sea，也见于 sea-bird、sea-wall 等复合词。

items.en: Wēod meant 'herb, grass, plant', with no hint of nuisance; the modern sense 'unwanted plant' developed later.
items.cn: wēod 意为「草、植物」，本无「有害」之意；现代「杂草」义是后来才发展出来的。

items.en: The compound sea + weed is recorded in the sixteenth century for plants of the sea; the exact first citation is not settled, so the date is approximate.
items.cn: sea + weed 的复合形式在 16 世纪有记录，指海中的植物；确切的最早书证尚无定论，因此年代为约数。

items.en: Modern botany limits seaweed to large algae; seagrasses are flowering plants and are therefore not seaweeds, a distinction everyday use often ignores.
items.cn: 现代植物学把 seaweed 限制为大型藻类；海草是开花植物，因此不算海藻，但日常用法常忽略这一区别。

items.en: From the nineteenth century seaweed was harvested for iodine and potash, and later for alginates, food and feed.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，海藻被采收用于制碘与钾碱，后来又用于褐藻胶、食品与饲料。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-English origin of weed is unsettled, and the earliest date of the compound is approximate rather than a fixed citation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：weed 在英语之前的来源没有定论，复合词的最早年代也只是约数，而非确切书证。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that are often mistaken for the same thing; group two holds words for edible sea plants that overlap without being synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是常被误认为同一种东西的形近词；第二组是可食海生植物的近义词，彼此重叠但并非同义。

entries.definition: Built from sea + -ward 'in the direction of', it means toward the sea and has nothing to do with weed.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sea + -ward「朝……方向」构成，意为朝海的方向，与 weed 无关。

entries.definition: A marine flowering plant with roots and flowers, not an alga; the name looks parallel but the biology is different.
entries.definitionCN: 有根有花的海洋开花植物，不是藻类；名称结构相似，但生物类别不同。

entries.definition: Wrack is seaweed, especially when washed ashore; sea wrack overlaps with seaweed but usually names the stranded mass.
entries.definitionCN: wrack 指海藻，尤指冲上岸的；sea wrack 与 seaweed 重叠，但通常指搁浅的那一堆。

entries.definition: Seaweed is the large, visible member of the algae; the group also contains single-celled forms never called seaweed.
entries.definitionCN: 海藻是藻类中大型、可见的成员；藻类还包括从不被称为 seaweed 的单细胞种类。

entries.definition: A kind of very large brown seaweed forming underwater forests; it is a seaweed, but not every seaweed is kelp.
entries.definitionCN: 一种形成海底森林的超大型褐藻；kelp 属于海藻，但并非所有海藻都是 kelp。

entries.definition: Seaweed of the shore, especially brown kinds cast up by the tide; the word stresses the stranded state.
entries.definitionCN: 岸边的海藻，尤指被潮水冲上岸的褐藻；这个词强调被搁浅的状态。

entries.definition: A Japanese term for dried laver sheets; it names one prepared food, while seaweed is the general material.
entries.definitionCN: 日语词，指干燥的紫菜片；它指一种成品食物，而 seaweed 是泛称的原料。

entries.definition: A red seaweed eaten dried in northern Europe; again a member of the seaweed family rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 北欧常晒干食用的一种红藻；同样是海藻家族的一员，而非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sea + weed: a plant-like growth of the sea, read literally.
normal.cn: sea + weed：字面就是「海里的草状生长物」。

normal.en: Seaweed is uncountable as a mass but countable as kinds: seaweed on the rocks, seaweeds of the tropics.
normal.cn: 作物质时不可数，作种类时可数：礁石上的 seaweed，热带的多种 seaweeds。

normal.en: Seagrass is not seaweed: it flowers, has roots, and belongs with land plants.
normal.cn: seagrass 不是 seaweed：它有花有根，属于陆生植物的近亲。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: seaweed extract, seaweed farming, seaweed soup, seaweed bed.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：海藻提取物、海藻养殖、海藻汤、海藻床。

normal.en: The industrial product alginate comes from brown seaweed, which links the food word to chemistry.
normal.cn: 工业产品 alginate 来自褐藻，这把食物词与化学连了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a green ribbon that keeps waving even after the wave has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿色的带子，浪走了它还在摆。

abstract.en: Picture a basket of the sea carried home on a woman's back.
abstract.cn: 想象一篮「海」被背回家。

abstract.en: Picture a tangled heap of nets that looks like it grew on the quay.
abstract.cn: 想象码头上一堆缠结的渔网，像是从岸上长出来的海藻。

examples.en: Seaweed on the rocks keeps the shore cool and wet at low tide.
examples.cn: 礁石上的海藻在退潮时为岸边保冷保湿。

examples.en: The farm grows seaweed for food and for alginate.
examples.cn: 这个养殖场养殖海藻，用于食用和提取褐藻胶。

examples.en: A thick layer of seaweed marked where the storm tide had reached.
examples.cn: 厚厚一层海藻标出了风暴潮抵达的位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: sea（海）+ weed（草）——海里的草就是海藻；看到礁石上的绿带子就想这个词

root: 英语本族复合词：sea（古英语 sǣ「海」）+ weed（古英语 wēod「草、植物」）；weed 的更深词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one material through its uses: the plant in the sea, the crop in the basket, the raw material in the factory, the mulch on the field, the wrack on the strand, the forest under water, the sheet on the plate, and finally the tangle in the harbour.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一种材料穿过各种用途：海里的植物、篮里的收成、厂里的原料、田里的肥料、滩上的搁浅物、水下的森林、盘上的薄片，最后是港口的缠结。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wet green ribbons hanging from rocks, water still dripping from them.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿漉漉的绿带子挂在礁石上，水还在往下滴。

branches.en: WHERE IT LIES: alive on the rock or dead on the strand, the word stays with the material.
branches.cn: 它在哪儿：活着长在石上，或死了搁在滩上，词都跟着这份材料走。

branches.en: FOOD: the harvest is eaten fresh, dried, or pressed into sheets.
branches.cn: 食物：收成可鲜食、晒干，或压成薄片。

branches.en: WORKING MATERIAL: factories extract gums, farms dig it into the soil.
branches.cn: 可用之材：工厂提炼胶质，农田把它翻进土里。

branches.en: HABITAT: a dense stand becomes a forest that shelters other life.
branches.cn: 栖息地：密集的一片成了庇护其他生命的森林。

branches.en: SHAPE ALONE: the figurative sense keeps only the long, wet, tangled look.
branches.cn: 只剩形态：比喻义只保留长、湿、缠结的样子。

intro.en: Seaweed is a compound, so its two free morphemes can be read separately and then recombined in other words.
intro.cn: seaweed 是复合词，两个自由语素可以分开读，再组合进别的词。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: sea and weed are native English words. The Latin-based relatives are algae, algal and alginate, borrowed separately.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁语：sea 与 weed 是英语本族词。以拉丁为源的亲属词 algae、algal、alginate 是另行借入的。

items.example: The compound names the place of growth.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的前半标出生长地点。

items.example: The second half names the plant-like growth.
items.exampleCN: 后半标出像植物的生长物。

items.example: Seaweed covered the rocks.
items.exampleCN: 海藻覆满了礁石。

items.example: The bay holds dozens of seaweeds.
items.exampleCN: 这个海湾有数十种海藻。

items.meaningCN: 带海藻味的；覆满海藻的
items.example: The cove was seaweedy at low tide.
items.exampleCN: 退潮时这个小湾到处是海藻。

items.meaning: a patch where seaweed grows thickly
items.example: Fish shelter in the seaweed bed.
items.exampleCN: 鱼在海藻床里躲避。

items.example: The lotion contains seaweed extract.
items.exampleCN: 这款乳液含海藻提取物。

items.example: Seaweed farming spread along the cold coast.
items.exampleCN: 海藻养殖在寒冷海岸推广开来。

definition_zh: 珊瑚；珊瑚虫群体；珊瑚色；珊瑚制品
definition_en: a stony material built by tiny sea polyps, the animal colony itself, or the pink-orange colour of the precious kind
core_image: 海底一丛粉橙色的枝状硬骨，枝端还伸着细小的白色触手
scene: 浅海潜水时，向导指着一丛粉橙色的枝状硬骨，说明那些细小的触手是仍在取食的珊瑚虫。 The guide pointed to a branching pink-orange coral whose tiny polyps were still feeding.
sceneCN: 这里 coral 指「由珊瑚虫群体建造的活体珊瑚」（第 1 个义项：活着的珊瑚虫群体）；句意为向导指向一丛仍在取食的粉橙色枝状珊瑚。

forms.label: 形容词（珊瑚的；珊瑚色的）

derivatives.zh: 珊瑚的；珊瑚色的；珊瑚藻

senses.title: The living colony of polyps
senses.definition: a colony of small sea animals that build a shared skeleton around themselves
senses.definitionCN: 由许多细小海生动物构成的群体，它们在自己周围建造共同的骨骼
senses.example: The guide pointed to a branching coral whose polyps were still feeding.
senses.exampleCN: 向导指着一丛仍在取食的枝状珊瑚。
senses.why: Naturalists first took coral for a plant; once it was shown to be an animal, the same word came to name the living colony.
senses.whyCN: 博物学家最初把珊瑚当作植物；一旦证明它是动物，同一个词就开始指活的群体。

senses.title: The hard stony skeleton
senses.definition: the limy skeleton left by a coral colony, often branching or dome-shaped
senses.definitionCN: 珊瑚群体留下的钙质骨骼，常呈枝状或穹顶状
senses.example: The beach was made of broken coral and shell.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海滩由碎珊瑚和贝壳构成。
senses.why: The skeleton outlasts the animal, so the word transferred from the builder to the built thing.
senses.whyCN: 骨骼比动物活得久，于是这个词从建造者转到了被建造物上。

senses.title: The framework of a reef
senses.definition: coral as the main builder that raises a reef structure in shallow tropical seas
senses.definitionCN: 在浅热带海域抬升出礁体结构的主要造礁珊瑚
senses.example: Coral slowly raised a barrier along the edge of the island.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚沿海岛边缘慢慢筑起一道堡礁。
senses.why: In geology coral names the construction material of the reef, not the animal that made it.
senses.whyCN: 在地质语境里，coral 指礁体的建筑材料，而不是造它的动物。

senses.title: Polished coral as a material
senses.definition: the hard red or pink coral cut and polished for use in objects
senses.definitionCN: 被切割打磨、用于制作器物的红色或粉色硬珊瑚
senses.example: The workshop set a piece of coral into a silver ring.
senses.exampleCN: 工坊把一块珊瑚嵌进银戒指。
senses.why: Once cut and polished, the skeleton becomes a gem-like material, and the word follows the trade.
senses.whyCN: 一旦切割打磨，骨骼就成了类宝石的材料，词义也随行业走。

senses.title: The orange-pink colour
senses.definition: a soft orange-pink colour like precious red coral
senses.definitionCN: 像贵重红珊瑚那样的柔和橙粉色
senses.example: The walls were painted a warm coral.
senses.exampleCN: 墙面被刷成温暖的珊瑚色。
senses.why: The colour name is a straightforward transfer: the hue is named after the object that supplied the dye-like shade.
senses.whyCN: 颜色名是直接的转喻：这种色调以提供它的物件命名。

senses.title: Coral as ornament
senses.definition: beads, carvings or jewellery made from coral
senses.definitionCN: 用珊瑚制成的珠子、雕件或首饰
senses.example: A string of coral hung at her throat.
senses.exampleCN: 她颈间挂着一串珊瑚。
senses.why: The material is metonymy for the finished object, a common path from stuff to ornament.
senses.whyCN: 材料转指成品，这是从「材质」到「饰物」的常见路径。

senses.title: Fossil coral in rock
senses.definition: the remains of ancient coral preserved in limestone or shale
senses.definitionCN: 保存在石灰岩或页岩中的古代珊瑚遗骸
senses.example: Fossil coral in the cliff shows that this desert was once a sea.
senses.exampleCN: 崖壁里的珊瑚化石说明这片沙漠曾是海洋。
senses.why: Palaeontology keeps the name because the fossil keeps the shape, even though the animal is long gone.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学沿用这个名字，因为化石保留了形态，尽管动物早已消失。

senses.title: A protective talisman
senses.definition: red coral worn or hung as a charm against misfortune, especially for children
senses.definitionCN: 被佩戴或悬挂以避邪的红珊瑚，尤用于儿童
senses.example: The grandmother tied a small coral to the child's wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母把一小块珊瑚系在孩子手腕上。
senses.why: Traditional belief gave the red material a protective power, so coral also names a charm rather than a substance.
senses.whyCN: 传统信仰赋予红色材料护佑之力，因此 coral 也指护身符，而不只是物质。

intro.en: Coral reached English through Old French from Latin, which had borrowed the word from Greek; the Greek source is not fully settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: coral 经古法语、拉丁语进入英语，拉丁语又是从希腊语借来的；希腊语的来源尚无定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Korallion was the name of the red coral of the Mediterranean. Its deeper origin is not established; a Semitic loan is a common hypothesis, not a proven fact.
items.cn: korallion 是地中海红珊瑚的名称。其更深来源没有定论；源自闪米特语是一种常见假说，并非已证事实。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as corallium and used it for the red skeletal material, which Romans carved into beads and charms.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 corallium，指红色的骨骼材料，罗马人把它雕成珠子和护符。

items.en: Old French coral carried the word into English in the twelfth century, at first for the precious red material rather than for a living animal.
items.cn: 古法语 coral 在 12 世纪把这个词带入英语，最初指贵重的红色材料，而非活体动物。

items.en: For centuries coral was classed as a sea plant; eighteenth-century naturalists showed that the polyps are animals, and the zoological sense followed.
items.cn: 数百年来珊瑚被归为海生植物；18 世纪的博物学家证明珊瑚虫是动物，动物学义随之出现。

items.en: The colour name coral, for the soft orange-pink of the precious material, became common in English dress and decoration writing.
items.cn: 指贵重材料那种柔和橙粉色的颜色名 coral，在英语服饰与装饰文字中逐渐通行。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Greek korallion has no agreed etymology, and the Semitic Origin hypothesis is one proposal among several, so no single source is asserted here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：希腊 korallion 没有公认的词源，闪米特语来源只是若干假说之一，此处不武断选定一种。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same coral stock that are easily interchanged; group two holds reef and shell words with neighbouring meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 coral 词族、容易互换的词；第二组是意义相邻的礁与壳类词。

entries.definition: The plural counts colonies or kinds; coral as a mass material stays singular.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式计数群体或种类；作物质材料时仍用单数 coral。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning of or like coral; as a noun it also names red coralline algae, a different organism.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为珊瑚的或似珊瑚的；作名词时还指珊瑚藻，那是另一种生物。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'like', so it describes a branching shape without claiming the material is coral.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -oid「像」构成，描述枝状形态，并不表示材料真是珊瑚。

entries.definition: A reef is the whole wave-resistant structure; coral is one builder within it, alongside algae and other organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 礁指整座抗浪结构；珊瑚只是其中的建造者之一，还有藻类及其他生物参与。

entries.definition: One coral animal is a polyp; coral names the colony and its skeleton, not the individual.
entries.definitionCN: 单个珊瑚动物叫 polyp；coral 指群体及其骨骼，而非单个个体。

entries.definition: A ridge of rock, sand or coral near the surface; it may be built by coral but need not be.
entries.definitionCN: 靠近水面的一道岩石、沙或珊瑚脊；它可以由珊瑚建造，但并非必然。

entries.definition: The hard outer case of a mollusc or other animal; coral is an internal skeleton built by a colony, not a shell.
entries.definitionCN: 软体动物等的外壳；珊瑚是群体建造的骨骼，不是外壳。

entries.definition: A rock made largely of calcium carbonate, often from coral and shell debris; it is the stone, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 主要由碳酸钙构成的岩石，常来自珊瑚与贝壳碎屑；它指岩石，不指动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Coral names both the animal colony and the stone it leaves behind, so context decides which is meant.
normal.cn: coral 既指活体群体，也指它留下的石头，靠上下文判断指哪一个。

normal.en: The colour coral is simply the colour of red coral, not a separate root.
normal.cn: 颜色义 coral 就是红珊瑚的颜色，并非另一个词根。

normal.en: Coral reef and coral island are fixed compounds; reef alone can be rock or sand.
normal.cn: coral reef 与 coral island 是固定复合词；单说 reef 则可能是岩礁或沙洲。

normal.en: Coralline and coralloid both start with coral but point to 'of coral' and 'like coral' respectively.
normal.cn: coralline 与 coralloid 都以 coral 开头，但分别指「珊瑚的」与「像珊瑚的」。

normal.en: Coral bleaching is the fixed phrase for the whitening that follows the loss of algal partners.
normal.cn: 珊瑚失去共生藻后变白，固定说法是 coral bleaching。

abstract.en: Picture a city built by animals that never leave home, each adding a room of stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由从不离家的动物建起的城市，每只都添一间石屋。

abstract.en: Picture a pink branch that is soft while alive and becomes jewellery when dead.
abstract.cn: 想象一根粉色的枝，活着时柔软，死后变成首饰。

abstract.en: Picture a desert cliff holding the shape of a sea that vanished.
abstract.cn: 想象一面沙漠崖壁里留着早已消失的海洋的形状。

examples.en: Coral grows only where the water stays warm and clear.
examples.cn: 珊瑚只在水温温暖、水质清澈的地方生长。

examples.en: The island is a ring of coral around a drowned crater.
examples.cn: 这座岛是一圈环绕着沉没火山口的珊瑚。

examples.en: She chose a coral dress for the summer wedding.
examples.cn: 她为夏季婚礼选了一条珊瑚色的裙子。

dict_mnemonic.text: coral 读起来像「口若」——珊瑚枝一条条张开小口，像在不停地开口吃东西

root: 希腊 korallion「红珊瑚」→ 拉丁 corallium → 古法语 coral；korallion 的更深来源不确定，闪米特语来源只是一种假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object from life to stone to symbol: the living colony, its skeleton, the reef it raises, the polished material, the colour, the ornament, the fossil, and the charm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一物件从生命走到石头再走到象征：活体群体、骨骼、抬升的礁、打磨的材料、颜色、饰品、化石与护符。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pink branching stone with tiny white tentacles at the tips.
core.cn: 核心意象：粉色的枝状石头，枝端伸出细小的白色触手。

branches.en: BUILDER AND BUILT: the colony makes the stone, then the stone outlasts the colony.
branches.cn: 建造者与被建造物：群体造出石头，石头又比群体活得久。

branches.en: CONSTRUCTION: in geology the material is the reef itself.
branches.cn: 建筑：在地质语境中，这种材料就是礁体。

branches.en: MATERIAL TO ORNAMENT: cutting and polishing turn skeleton into gem and then into jewellery.
branches.cn: 从材料到饰品：切割打磨把骨骼变成宝石，再变成首饰。

branches.en: COLOUR BY METONYMY: the hue is named directly after the precious red kind.
branches.cn: 转喻得色：色调直接以贵重的红珊瑚命名。

branches.en: FROM STONE TO SYMBOL: the fossil proves an ancient sea, the charm promises protection.
branches.cn: 从石到象征：化石证明古海，护符许诺护佑。

intro.en: Coral is a borrowed noun with no productive English prefix; its family is built by compounding and by the suffixes -ine and -oid.
intro.cn: coral 是借入名词，没有能产的英语前缀；其词族靠复合与后缀 -ine、-oid 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin corallium and Greek korallion are the source forms; corallum is the Latin noun used in natural history for a coral colony.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 corallium 与希腊 korallion 是来源形式；corallum 是博物学中用于指珊瑚群体的拉丁名词。

items.meaning: red coral, and later any coral
items.meaningCN: 红珊瑚；后泛指各类珊瑚
items.example: Coral was once classed as a plant.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚曾被归为植物。

items.example: The reef holds hundreds of corals.
items.exampleCN: 这座礁有数百种珊瑚。

items.example: Coralline means belonging to coral.
items.exampleCN: coralline 意为属于珊瑚的。

items.meaning: of coral; also a red coralline alga
items.example: Coralline algae cement the reef frame.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚藻把礁体胶结起来。

items.example: The suffix marks resemblance, not identity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记相似，而非同一。

items.example: The mineral forms coralloid branches.
items.exampleCN: 这种矿物形成珊瑚状的枝。

items.meaning: a reef built chiefly by coral
items.example: The coral reef shelters the lagoon.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁护住了潟湖。

items.meaning: an island made largely of coral
items.example: Coral islands rise only a few metres above the sea.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚岛只高出海面几米。

items.example: The corallum is the whole skeletal frame.
items.exampleCN: corallum 指整个骨骼框架。

definition_zh: 珊瑚礁（由珊瑚骨骼堆积而成、接近海面的礁体及其生态系统）
definition_en: a ridge or platform near the sea surface built mainly by coral, together with the community that lives on it
core_image: 清透的浅海上，一道浅色的脊把深蓝与碧绿分开，脊上布满枝状与块状的珊瑚
scene: 小船驶进清透的浅海，船底突然出现一道浅色的脊，把深蓝的水与碧绿的水分开。 A coral reef lay just beneath the hull, its top within reach of the sunlight.
sceneCN: 这里 coral reef 指「接近海面、由珊瑚建造的礁体」（第 1 个义项：珊瑚骨骼堆成的浅海礁脊）；句意为船底正下方就是一道顶部能被阳光照到的珊瑚礁。

derivatives.zh: 礁坪（礁体顶部的浅平区）

senses.title: A ridge built by coral near the surface
senses.definition: a stony ridge or platform in shallow tropical water, raised by the accumulated skeletons of coral
senses.definitionCN: 在浅热带海域由珊瑚骨骼堆积抬升而成的石质脊或平台
senses.example: A coral reef lay just beneath the hull.
senses.exampleCN: 船底正下方就是一道珊瑚礁。
senses.why: Coral supplies the builder and reef supplies the shape, so the compound names a structure defined by what made it.
senses.whyCN: coral 提供建造者，reef 提供形状，因此这个复合词按「由什么造成」来定义一种结构。

senses.title: The community living on the structure
senses.definition: the dense community of fish, invertebrates and algae that depends on the reef framework
senses.definitionCN: 依赖礁体结构生存的鱼类、无脊椎动物与藻类群落
senses.example: The coral reef supports more species than the open sea around it.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁支撑的物种比周围开阔海更多。
senses.why: Ecology names the habitat by its frame, so the phrase shifts from stone to the life that occupies it.
senses.whyCN: 生态学以框架来命名栖息地，于是这个短语从石头转向占据它的生命。

senses.title: A charted hazard to navigation
senses.titleCN: 海图上标出的航行障碍
senses.definition: a shallow reef marked on charts because it can damage a hull
senses.definitionCN: 在海图上标出、可能损伤船体的浅礁
senses.example: The chart marks the coral reef two miles offshore.
senses.exampleCN: 海图在离岸两英里处标出了这道珊瑚礁。
senses.why: For sailors the reef is first of all an obstruction, so the phrase enters navigation language as a warning.
senses.whyCN: 对水手来说礁首先是障碍，因此这个短语以警告的身份进入航海语言。

senses.title: An ancient reef now in rock
senses.titleCN: 如今留在岩层中的古礁
senses.definition: the fossilized structure of a former coral reef, often preserved as limestone
senses.definitionCN: 旧日珊瑚礁被石化后的结构，常以石灰岩形式保存
senses.example: An ancient coral reef now stands inland as a low ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一道古代珊瑚礁如今作为低矮的山脊立在内陆。
senses.why: Geology reads the same structure in stone, so the phrase survives the death of the entire community.
senses.whyCN: 地质学在石头里读出同一结构，因此这个短语在整片群落死亡之后仍然存在。

senses.title: A resource for tourism and fishing
senses.definition: a reef valued as a dive site or fishing ground that brings income
senses.definitionCN: 作为潜水点或渔场而带来收入的礁
senses.example: Divers travel thousands of miles to see that coral reef.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水者远行千里只为看那道珊瑚礁。
senses.why: The phrase turns into an economic asset once people pay to visit or harvest from it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们付费到访或从中捕捞，这个短语就变成经济资产。

senses.title: A unit of conservation
senses.definition: a reef managed as a protected area, with rules on fishing and anchoring
senses.definitionCN: 作为保护区管理、对捕捞与抛锚设有规定的礁
senses.example: The marine park covers three coral reefs and their lagoons.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋公园涵盖三道珊瑚礁及其潟湖。
senses.why: Conservation needs countable units, and a whole reef becomes one manageable object.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作需要有可数的单元，一整道礁于是成为一个可管理的对象。

senses.title: A type in the fringing-barrier-atoll series
senses.titleCN: 裙礁—堡礁—环礁序列中的类型
senses.definition: one of the standard forms of reef, classed by its relation to a coast or lagoon
senses.definitionCN: 按与海岸或潟湖的关系划分的标准礁型之一
senses.example: A barrier coral reef rings the island at some distance from the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 一道堡礁在离岸较远处环抱这座岛。
senses.why: Darwin's classification turned reefs into types, and the compound is used with fringing, barrier and atoll.
senses.whyCN: 达尔文的分类把礁分成类型，这个复合词常与 fringing、barrier、atoll 搭配使用。

senses.title: A dense, sheltering structure, figuratively
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：密集而能藏身的结构
senses.definition: a crowded, branching structure that offers many niches and hiding places, compared to a reef
senses.definitionCN: 像珊瑚礁那样密集分枝、提供许多小生境与藏身处的结构
senses.example: The old market was a coral reef of stalls where a stranger could disappear.
senses.exampleCN: 旧市场像一片珊瑚礁，摊位密集，陌生人一进去就不见了。
senses.why: The figurative use keeps the reef's two features, dense growth and many hiding places, and drops the water.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义保留礁的两个特征——密集生长与众多藏身处，只去掉海水。

intro.en: Coral reef joins a Greek-derived noun of uncertain origin to an Old Norse word for a sea ridge; the compound is modern, the parts are old. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: coral reef 把一个来源不确定的希腊系名词与一个古诺斯语「海脊」词连在一起；复合词是近代的，两部分都很古老。年代均为约数。

items.en: Coral comes from Greek korallion, the red coral of the Mediterranean. The Greek word's deeper origin is not established; a Semitic loan is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.cn: coral 来自希腊 korallion，指地中海红珊瑚。这个希腊词的更深来源没有定论；源自闪米特语只是一种假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Latin corallium and Old French coral carried the word to English, first as the precious red material rather than as a reef-building animal.
items.cn: 拉丁 corallium 与古法语 coral 把这个词带到英语，最初指贵重的红色材料，而非造礁动物。

items.en: Reef comes from Old Norse rif, 'ridge at sea', the same shape-word used for a rib; whether the sea sense grew from 'rib' or from a 'tearing' verb is debated.
items.cn: reef 来自古诺斯语 rif「海中的脊」，与表示「肋骨」的是同一个形状词；海义究竟由「肋骨」还是由某个「撕裂」动词发展而来，仍有争论。

items.en: Coral reef is recorded from the eighteenth century, when Pacific and Indian Ocean voyagers began charting shallow coral structures.
items.cn: coral reef 自 18 世纪有记录，当时太平洋与印度洋的航海者开始测绘浅水珊瑚结构。

items.en: Darwin's 1842 book on coral reefs fixed the familiar series fringing reef, barrier reef and atoll, and the compound entered general science with it.
items.cn: 达尔文 1842 年关于珊瑚礁的著作确立了裙礁、堡礁、环礁这一熟悉序列，这个复合词也随之进入通用科学语。

items.en: Source uncertain (both parts): korallion has no agreed etymology, and the relation of rif to 'rib' and to 'tear' remains unsettled; exact first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（两部分皆是）：korallion 没有公认词源，rif 与「肋骨」「撕裂」的关系亦无定论；确切首见年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds the parts and near-spellings of the phrase itself; group two holds other shallow-water structures that are often confused with a coral reef.
note.cn: 第一组是这个短语自身的组成部分与形近词；第二组是常与珊瑚礁混淆的其他浅水结构。

entries.definition: The animal and its skeleton; a coral reef is the structure, so the two words are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物及其骨骼；珊瑚礁是整体结构，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: Any ridge near the surface, of rock, sand or coral; without coral it may still be a reef but not a coral reef.
entries.definitionCN: 任何接近水面的岩、沙或珊瑚脊；没有珊瑚时仍可称礁，但不能称珊瑚礁。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning of or like coral; it also names red algae that cement reefs but are not coral.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为珊瑚的或似珊瑚的；也指胶结礁体的红藻，但那些藻不是珊瑚。

entries.definition: An island built of coral debris and sand; it may sit on a reef, but the phrase names dry land rather than the submerged structure.
entries.definitionCN: 由珊瑚碎屑与沙堆成的岛；它可能坐落在礁上，但这个短语指陆地，而非水下结构。

entries.definition: A coral reef forming a ring around a lagoon; an atoll is one type of coral reef, not a synonym for all of them.
entries.definitionCN: 环绕潟湖成环的珊瑚礁；环礁是珊瑚礁的一种类型，并非所有珊瑚礁的同义词。

entries.definition: A reef running parallel to a coast with a lagoon between; it is a coral reef in a particular position.
entries.definitionCN: 与海岸平行、中间隔有潟湖的礁；它是处在特定位置的珊瑚礁。

entries.definition: A shallow bank of sand or rock that hazards ships; it need not be built by coral and need not break the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 危及船只的浅沙洲或浅岩滩；它未必由珊瑚建造，也未必露出水面。

entries.definition: A small low island of sand on a reef; the reef is the structure beneath, the cay is the dry patch above.
entries.definitionCN: 礁上低矮的小沙岛；礁是下面的结构，cay 是上面的干出部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: coral names the builder, reef names the ridge: together they name a structure and its maker.
normal.cn: coral 标建造者，reef 标脊状结构：合起来就是结构与制造者。

normal.en: The plural is coral reefs, with the -s on reef, not on coral.
normal.cn: 复数是 coral reefs，-s 加在 reef 上，不加在 coral 上。

normal.en: Darwin's three types are fringing reef, barrier reef and atoll, all of them coral reefs.
normal.cn: 达尔文的三类是裙礁、堡礁、环礁，三者都是珊瑚礁。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: coral reef ecosystem, coral reef conservation, coral reef bleaching.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：珊瑚礁生态系统、珊瑚礁保护、珊瑚礁白化。

normal.en: A cay is dry sand on a reef; a shoal is shallow but not necessarily coral.
normal.cn: cay 是礁上的干沙；shoal 是浅滩，但未必由珊瑚构成。

abstract.en: Picture a pale line in blue water where waves break before they reach the shore.
abstract.cn: 想象蓝色水面上一条浅色的线，浪在到岸之前先在那里碎开。

abstract.en: Picture a stone city under water, every window filled with a fish.
abstract.cn: 想象一座水下石城，每个窗口里都有一条鱼。

abstract.en: Picture a market so crowded that it hides anyone who walks in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个拥挤到能把走进的人藏起来的市场。

examples.en: The coral reef absorbs wave energy before it reaches the beach.
examples.cn: 珊瑚礁在波浪到达海滩之前吸收其能量。

examples.en: Sediment from the cleared hillside smothered the coral reef below.
examples.cn: 被清空的山坡冲下的泥沙把下面的珊瑚礁埋住了。

examples.en: Scientists survey the coral reef every year to count fish and bleached colonies.
examples.cn: 科学家每年调查这片珊瑚礁，统计鱼类与白化的珊瑚群体。

dict_mnemonic.text: coral（珊瑚）+ reef（礁）——珊瑚搭起来的礁就是珊瑚礁；把两个词连起来记最省力

root: coral（希腊 korallion「红珊瑚」，更深来源不确定）+ reef（古诺斯语 rif「海中的脊」）；两词在英语中合为复合名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the structure itself to what lives on it and what people do with it: ridge, community, hazard, fossil, resource, protected unit, reef type and finally a metaphor for any crowded shelter.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从结构本身移向栖居其上的生命与人的利用：礁脊、群落、航行障碍、化石、资源、保护单元、礁型，最后是任何密集庇护所的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale ridge in clear water, splitting deep blue from turquoise.
core.cn: 核心意象：清透水中的一道浅色脊，把深蓝与碧绿分开。

branches.en: FORM: whatever its type, the object is a ridge raised by coral.
branches.cn: 形态：无论哪一类型，这个对象都是珊瑚抬升出的脊。

branches.en: LIFE: the stone becomes a habitat, and the phrase names the community too.
branches.cn: 生命：石头变成栖息地，短语也指其中的群落。

branches.en: USE AND DANGER: the same ridge is an asset to divers and a hazard to hulls.
branches.cn: 利用与危险：同一道脊对潜水者是资源，对船体是危险。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: the fossil reef keeps the shape after the sea is gone.
branches.cn: 深时：海水退去后，化石礁仍保留形状。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT AND METAPHOR: a countable unit to protect, and a crowded shelter to imagine.
branches.cn: 管理与比喻：既是可保护的单位，也是可想象的密集庇护所。

intro.en: Coral reef is a two-noun compound, so its morphology is compounding rather than prefixation; each half still has its own family.
intro.cn: coral reef 是双名词复合词，其构词方式是复合而非加前缀；两半各自仍有自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Only coral has a Latin source, corallium; reef is Germanic, from Old Norse rif, so the compound joins two different language stocks.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 coral 有拉丁来源 corallium；reef 属日耳曼语，来自古诺斯语 rif，因此这个复合词连接了两个不同的语源。

items.structure: Old French coral, from Latin corallium
items.example: Coral supplies the building material.
items.exampleCN: coral 提供建筑材料。

items.example: Reef supplies the shape.
items.exampleCN: reef 提供形状。

items.meaning: a coral-built ridge near the surface
items.example: The coral reef shelters the bay.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁护住了海湾。

items.example: Coral reefs ring the archipelago.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁环绕着群岛。

items.structure: coral reef used as a modifier
items.example: Coral-reef fish rarely stray into open water.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁鱼类很少游到开阔水域。

items.meaning: the shallow top surface of a reef
items.example: The reef flat dries at extreme low tide.
items.exampleCN: 极低潮时礁坪会露出水面。

items.meaning: the raised outer edge of a reef
items.example: Waves break hardest on the reef crest.
items.exampleCN: 浪在礁缘碎得最猛。

items.meaning: coral species that raise reef frameworks
items.example: Reef-building coral needs clear warm water.
items.exampleCN: 造礁珊瑚需要清澈温暖的水。

definition_en: a ridge of rock, sand or coral near the surface of the sea, a vein of ore in rock, or to shorten a sail
core_image: 海面下一道浅色的脊，浪在它上面碎成一条白线
scene: 帆船驶近浅水区，船长看见船首方向有一道浅色的脊，浪在它上面碎成一条白线。 The captain saw a pale reef breaking the swell ahead of the bow.
sceneCN: 这里 reef 指「接近水面、使浪破碎的岩脊或珊瑚脊」（第 1 个义项：海面下的礁脊）；句意为船长看见船首前方有一道浅色的礁脊正在把涌浪打碎。

senses.title: A ridge of rock near the surface
senses.definition: a line of rock, sand or coral lying close enough to the surface to break waves
senses.definitionCN: 接近水面、足以使波浪破碎的一道岩石、沙或珊瑚脊
senses.example: The captain saw a pale reef breaking the swell.
senses.exampleCN: 船长看见一道浅色的礁脊把涌浪打碎。
senses.why: The core sense is a shape, not a material: whatever lies near enough to the surface to disturb the water is a reef.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是形状而非材料：任何接近水面、足以扰动水流的物体都算 reef。

senses.title: A coral-built reef
senses.definition: a reef whose frame was raised by coral colonies in warm shallow seas
senses.definitionCN: 在温暖浅海中由珊瑚群体抬升出的礁体
senses.example: The reef grew slowly as the coral colonies stacked their skeletons.
senses.exampleCN: 随着珊瑚群体堆积骨骼，这道礁慢慢长高。
senses.why: Coral is the most famous reef builder, so in ordinary use reef often implies coral even when the word does not say so.
senses.whyCN: 珊瑚是最著名的造礁者，因此日常用法中 reef 常暗指珊瑚，尽管词面并未说明。

senses.title: A hazard shown on charts
senses.titleCN: 海图上标出的航行障碍
senses.definition: a shallow reef that endangers ships and is therefore marked on nautical charts
senses.definitionCN: 危及船只、因此在海图上标出的浅礁
senses.example: The reef lies exactly where the old chart shows no depth.
senses.exampleCN: 这道暗礁正好位于旧海图没有标注深度的位置。
senses.why: Navigation cares about depth, so reef becomes a warning category rather than a geological one.
senses.whyCN: 航海关心的是深度，因此 reef 成了警告类别，而非地质类别。

senses.title: A vein of ore in rock
senses.definition: a gold-bearing or mineral-bearing vein running through rock, especially in mining districts
senses.definitionCN: 贯穿岩石的含金或含矿脉体，尤见于采矿区
senses.example: Miners followed the gold reef deep into the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工沿着含金矿脉深入山体。
senses.why: Mining borrowed the image of a long ridge and applied it underground, where the ore also runs in a line.
senses.whyCN: 采矿借用了「长脊」的形象用于地下，因为矿体也呈线状延伸。

senses.title: To shorten a sail
senses.definition: to reduce the area of a sail by folding or tying part of it down
senses.definitionCN: 通过折叠或系扎帆的一部分来减小受风面积
senses.example: The crew reefed the mainsail as the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 风起时船员缩了主帆。
senses.why: The verb is a separate nautical borrowing, probably from Dutch; it shares spelling with the rock but not the same origin path.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是另一条航海借词线，可能来自荷兰语；它与岩石义拼写相同，但来源路径不同。

senses.title: The reef knot
senses.definition: a flat knot used to tie two ends of a line, traditionally used when reefing sails
senses.definitionCN: 用来连接两段绳端的扁平结，传统上用于缩帆
senses.example: He finished with a reef knot that would not slip under load.
senses.exampleCN: 他最后打了一个受力也不滑的平结。
senses.why: The knot is named for the sail-reefing job it was used for, so here reef refers to the sailor's action, not the rock.
senses.whyCN: 这种结因其缩帆用途得名，因此这里的 reef 指水手的动作，而非岩石。

senses.title: A barrier, figuratively
senses.definition: an unseen obstacle that suddenly blocks progress
senses.definitionCN: 突然阻挡进展的隐蔽障碍
senses.example: The talks hit a reef of unresolved property claims.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈撞上了未解决的产权主张这块暗礁。
senses.why: A reef is hidden just under the surface and strikes without warning, which is exactly the figurative point.
senses.whyCN: 暗礁藏在水面之下、毫无预警地撞上来，这正是比喻的要害。

senses.title: A surfing wave over rock
senses.definition: a wave that breaks over a shallow rock or coral bottom, producing a steep, fast ride
senses.definitionCN: 在浅岩或珊瑚底上破碎、形成陡而快的浪
senses.example: Surfers prefer the reef because the wave holds its shape.
senses.exampleCN: 冲浪者偏爱这处礁石浪，因为浪形保持得久。
senses.why: Surfing culture names a spot by its bottom, so reef came to mean a particular kind of breaking wave.
senses.whyCN: 冲浪文化用海底类型给浪点命名，于是 reef 也指一种特定的破碎浪。

intro.en: Reef is a Scandinavian borrowing for a sea ridge; the sailing verb is a separate nautical loan, and the mining sense grew from the same ridge image. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: reef 是来自斯堪的纳维亚语、表示海中脊的借词；缩帆动词是另一条航海借词线，采矿义则由同一「脊」的形象发展而来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Rif meant 'rib' and also 'ridge at sea'. Whether the sea sense grew out of the body-part word or from a verb meaning 'to tear' is debated, so the link is probable rather than proven.
items.cn: rif 既指「肋骨」，也指「海中的脊」。海义是由身体部位词发展而来，还是来自某个意为「撕裂」的动词，尚有争论，因此这种联系只是很可能，而非已证。

items.en: The noun enters English in the sixteenth century, first in sailing and charting accounts of northern waters.
items.cn: 这个名词在 16 世纪进入英语，最初见于北方海域的航行与测深记述。

items.en: The verb 'to reef a sail' appears in the seventeenth century and is usually taken as a separate borrowing, probably from Dutch reven; the shared spelling is accidental.
items.cn: 「缩帆」动词出现于 17 世纪，一般认为是另一条借词线，可能来自荷兰语 reven；拼写相同属偶然。

items.en: In the nineteenth century gold fields from Australia to South Africa called a mineral-bearing vein a reef, extending the ridge image underground.
items.cn: 19 世纪，从澳大利亚到南非的金矿都把含矿脉称作 reef，把「脊」的形象延伸到地下。

items.en: Coral reef as a fixed compound spread in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries with Pacific exploration and Darwin's classification.
items.cn: coral reef 作为固定复合词，随太平洋探险与达尔文分类在 18、19 世纪传播开来。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the relation of rif to 'rib' and to 'tear' is unsettled, and the Dutch origin of the sailing verb is a likely reconstruction rather than a documented fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：rif 与「肋骨」「撕裂」的关系没有定论，缩帆动词的荷兰语来源也只是较可信的推测，并非有文献确证的事实。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical spellings with unrelated meanings; group two holds shallow-water and shoreline features that are often used as if interchangeable with reef.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写极近而意义无关的词；第二组是常被当作 reef 同义词使用的浅水与岸线地貌词。

entries.definition: A short repeated phrase in music; it is a different word with no path to the sea ridge.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐中反复演奏的短句；这是另一个词，与海中脊无关。

entries.definition: A crack or tear, from a verb meaning to split; it is not reef, and it describes a gap rather than a rise.
entries.definitionCN: 裂缝或撕裂，来自意为「裂开」的动词；它不是 reef，描述的是凹陷而非隆起。

entries.definition: Old Norse rif meant both rib and sea ridge, so rib may be a distant relative rather than a false friend.
entries.definitionCN: 古诺斯语 rif 既指肋骨也指海中脊，因此 rib 可能是远亲，而非纯然的假朋友。

entries.definition: A nautical word for a sailor or a short jacket, tied historically to reefing sails; it is not a reef itself.
entries.definitionCN: 航海词，指水手或短外套，历史上与缩帆有关；它本身不是礁。

entries.definition: A shallow bank of sand or mud that hazards navigation; it is defined by depth, not by coral or rock.
entries.definitionCN: 危及航行的浅沙洲或泥滩；它以深度定义，而非以珊瑚或岩石定义。

entries.definition: A ridge of sand built by currents, often exposed at low tide; unlike a reef it is loose sediment, not rock or coral.
entries.definitionCN: 由水流堆成的沙脊，低潮时常露出；与礁不同，它是松散沉积物，不是岩石或珊瑚。

entries.definition: A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon; an atoll is a kind of reef, so the words are related by type.
entries.definitionCN: 围出潟湖的环状珊瑚礁；环礁是礁的一种，两词是类型关系。

entries.definition: A low sandy island on a reef; it is land, while the reef is the submerged structure that supports it.
entries.definitionCN: 礁上的低矮沙岛；它是陆地，而礁是支撑它的水下结构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Reef is a shape word first: a ridge near the surface that makes waves break.
normal.cn: reef 首先是形状词：接近水面、使浪破碎的一道脊。

normal.en: Coral reef, barrier reef, reef flat and reef crest all build on the same ridge image.
normal.cn: coral reef、barrier reef、reef flat、reef crest 都建立在同一个「脊」的形象上。

normal.en: Reef the sails and reef knot belong to the sailor's reef, not to the rock.
normal.cn: reef the sails 与 reef knot 属于水手的 reef 义，与岩石义不同。

normal.en: Gold reef extends the ridge image into mining: a line of ore in rock.
normal.cn: gold reef 把脊的形象延伸到采矿：岩层中呈线状的矿体。

normal.en: Reef as a hazard is hidden just below the surface, which is why it became a metaphor for unseen trouble.
normal.cn: 作为障碍的 reef 藏在水面之下，因此成了「看不见的麻烦」的比喻。

abstract.en: Picture a white line of foam where the sea suddenly shallows.
abstract.cn: 想象海水突然变浅处那条白色的泡沫线。

abstract.en: Picture a line of gold running through dark rock like a ridge under water.
abstract.cn: 想象一条金线穿过暗色岩石，像水下的脊。

abstract.en: Picture a boat talking to the sea by folding its sail.
abstract.cn: 想象一条船通过折叠帆来与海对话。

examples.en: The reef lies a metre below the surface at low tide.
examples.cn: 低潮时这道礁位于水面下一米。

examples.en: They reefed the sails before the squall reached the boat.
examples.cn: 在飑线到达船之前，他们缩了帆。

examples.en: The mine worked a narrow reef of gold-bearing quartz.
examples.cn: 这座矿开采一条狭窄的含金石英脉。

dict_mnemonic.text: reef 读起来像「锐夫」——水下的脊很「锐」，把浪割成白线；记「暗礁」先想那条白线

root: 古诺斯语 rif「海中的脊」，与「肋骨」同形；其与「撕裂」的联系属推测；缩帆义另经荷兰语航海词传入，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape through different worlds: the rock under the wave, the coral that builds it, the chart that warns of it, the ore vein underground, the sail shortened, the knot tied, the obstacle unseen, and the wave that surfers seek.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个形状穿过不同世界：浪下的岩脊、造它的珊瑚、标出它的海图、地下的矿脉、缩起的帆、系好的结、看不见的障碍，以及冲浪者追逐的浪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale ridge just under the water, with a white line of foam above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：水面下不远处一道浅色的脊，上方是一条白色泡沫线。

branches.en: RIDGE AND BUILDER: a shape in the sea, made most famously by coral.
branches.cn: 脊与建造者：海中的一个形状，最著名的制造者是珊瑚。

branches.en: BREAKING WATER: the same shallow top warns sailors and attracts surfers.
branches.cn: 碎浪：同一个浅顶既警告水手，也吸引冲浪者。

branches.en: UNDERGROUND RIDGE: mining moves the line of rock beneath the surface.
branches.cn: 地下之脊：采矿把这条岩石线移到地表之下。

branches.en: SAILOR'S REEF: a separate nautical word for shortening sail and the knot used to do it.
branches.cn: 水手的 reef：另一条航海词义，指缩帆以及缩帆所用的结。

branches.en: HIDDEN OBSTACLE: what is just under the surface strikes without warning.
branches.cn: 隐蔽障碍：藏在水面下的东西毫无预警地撞上来。

intro.en: Reef is a bare noun with no prefix; its family grows by plural, verb endings and compounding.
intro.cn: reef 是没有前缀的单纯名词；其词族靠复数、动词词尾与复合构成。

latinIntro.en: Reef has no Latin source; it is Scandinavian. Latin-based sea words such as coral, marine and littoral are separate borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: reef 没有拉丁来源，属斯堪的纳维亚语；coral、marine、littoral 等拉丁系海词是另外的借词。

items.example: The noun names the ridge itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词指脊本身。

items.example: The strait is full of reefs.
items.exampleCN: 这条海峡布满暗礁。

items.example: They sailed on with reefed sails.
items.exampleCN: 他们缩着帆继续航行。

items.meaning: the act of shortening a sail
items.example: Reefing took only a minute.
items.exampleCN: 缩帆只用了一分钟。

items.example: The reefy channel needs a local pilot.
items.exampleCN: 这条多礁水道需要本地引航员。

items.meaning: a flat knot used in reefing
items.example: Tie the bundle with a reef knot.
items.exampleCN: 用平结把包裹捆好。

items.meaning: the shallow top of a reef
items.example: The reef flat is exposed at low tide.
items.exampleCN: 低潮时礁坪露出水面。

items.meaning: a wave breaking over a reef
items.example: The reef break is fast and shallow.
items.exampleCN: 这处礁石浪又快又浅。

items.example: The coral reef protects the harbour.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁护住了港口。

definition_zh: 软体动物（身体柔软、通常带壳的无脊椎动物）
definition_en: a soft-bodied invertebrate, usually protected by a shell, such as a snail, oyster or squid
core_image: 一枚湿亮的螺壳贴在礁石上，壳口探出一小段柔软的身体
scene: 退潮后的礁石上，一只螺用宽大的软足慢慢爬行，背上的螺壳随身体一起移动。 A mollusk crept across the wet rock, its soft foot gripping the surface beneath a spiral shell.
sceneCN: 这里 mollusk 指「软体动物」（第 1 个义项：身体柔软、通常带壳的无脊椎动物）；句意为一枚软体动物靠柔软的足在湿岩上爬行，背上背着螺壳。

senses.title: A member of the phylum Mollusca
senses.titleCN: 软体动物门的一个成员
senses.definition: any invertebrate of the large phylum Mollusca, with a soft body, a muscular foot and usually a shell
senses.definitionCN: 软体动物门中任何身体柔软、有肌肉质足、通常带壳的无脊椎动物
senses.example: A mollusk crept across the wet rock beneath a spiral shell.
senses.exampleCN: 一枚软体动物背着螺壳在湿岩上爬行。
senses.why: The name comes from Latin for 'soft', because the body is soft even when the shell is hard.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自拉丁语「柔软」，因为即使壳很硬，身体本身仍是软的。

senses.title: A mollusk eaten as food
senses.definition: an edible mollusk such as a mussel, oyster or scallop
senses.definitionCN: 可食用的软体动物，如贻贝、牡蛎或扇贝
senses.example: The market sells mollusks by the basket.
senses.exampleCN: 市场成篮地卖贝类。
senses.why: Fisheries use the biological word for the catch, so mollusk also names a food category.
senses.whyCN: 渔业用这个生物学词来指渔获，因此 mollusk 也成了一个食品类别。

senses.title: The animal that makes a shell
senses.definition: the living animal whose mantle secretes the calcareous shell found on beaches
senses.definitionCN: 由外套膜分泌钙质外壳、其壳常被冲上海滩的活体动物
senses.example: Every shell on the beach was made by a mollusk.
senses.exampleCN: 海滩上的每一枚贝壳都由软体动物造出。
senses.why: Seashells are the most familiar trace of these animals, so the word is often learned through the shell rather than the body.
senses.whyCN: 贝壳是这类动物最熟悉的痕迹，因此人们常先认识壳，再认识动物。

senses.title: A garden or crop pest
senses.definition: a snail or slug that damages plants and is controlled by gardeners
senses.definitionCN: 损害植物、需由园丁防治的螺或蛞蝓
senses.example: Slugs are mollusks that strip young seedlings overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 蛞蝓是软体动物，一夜之间就能把幼苗啃光。
senses.why: The same phylum includes shell-less garden pests, so the word reaches beyond the sea.
senses.whyCN: 同一门类里还有无壳的园圃害虫，因此这个词的适用范围超出了海洋。

senses.title: A fossil used in dating rock
senses.definition: an ancient mollusk preserved in rock, often used as an index fossil for relative dating
senses.definitionCN: 保存在岩石中的古代软体动物，常用作相对定年的标准化石
senses.example: The limestone layer is dated by the mollusks inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 这层石灰岩靠其中的软体动物化石定年。
senses.why: Mollusks evolved quickly and spread widely, which makes their fossils useful clocks.
senses.whyCN: 软体动物演化快、分布广，因此它们的化石成了好用的时钟。

senses.title: An intermediate host for parasites
senses.definition: a snail in whose body a parasitic worm passes one stage of its life cycle
senses.definitionCN: 寄生虫在其体内度过一个生活史阶段的螺
senses.example: The disease spreads through a freshwater mollusk.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病通过一种淡水螺传播。
senses.why: Public health texts name the snail simply as a mollusk when describing the transmission chain.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生文献在描述传播链时，常直接把这个螺称为 mollusk。

senses.title: A laboratory model animal
senses.definition: a mollusk used in research, especially the squid for studies of nerve conduction
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究的软体动物，尤指用于神经传导研究的鱿鱼
senses.example: The squid giant axon made a mollusk central to neuroscience.
senses.exampleCN: 鱿鱼的巨大轴突使一种软体动物成为神经科学的核心。
senses.why: The squid's unusually large nerve fibre made a mollusk the easiest animal in which to measure a nerve impulse.
senses.whyCN: 鱿鱼异常粗大的神经纤维，使一种软体动物成为最容易测量神经冲动的动物。

senses.title: A farmed or invasive species
senses.definition: a mollusk cultivated for food or one that has spread beyond its native range
senses.definitionCN: 为食用而养殖、或已扩散到原分布区之外的软体动物
senses.example: The Pacific oyster is a mollusk farmed on every continent.
senses.exampleCN: 太平洋牡蛎是一种在各大洲都养殖的软体动物。
senses.why: Aquaculture and invasion biology both need a neutral group label, and mollusk supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 水产养殖与入侵生物学都需要一个中性的类群标签，mollusk 正好提供。

intro.en: Mollusk goes back to Latin mollis 'soft' through the adjective molluscus; it is a scientific borrowing that replaced older popular names. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mollusk 经形容词 molluscus 上溯到拉丁 mollis「柔软」；它是科学借词，取代了更早的通俗名称。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mollis meant 'soft, tender, pliant', and molluscus meant 'soft, soft-shelled'. The deeper Indo-European root proposed for mollis is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mollis 意为「柔软的、柔韧的」，molluscus 意为「软的、软壳的」。为 mollis 提出的更早印欧词根属重构形式。

items.en: French naturalists used mollusque for this group in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and English borrowed the term from French.
items.cn: 法国博物学家在 17、18 世纪用 mollusque 指这个类群，英语从法语借入该词。

items.en: Greek natural history had grouped soft-bodied sea animals under a word meaning 'soft things'; Latin mollusca continued that idea rather than inventing it.
items.cn: 希腊自然史早已用意为「柔软之物」的词来归拢身体柔软的海生动物；拉丁 mollusca 延续了这一思路，而非凭空创造。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century zoology fixed Mollusca as a major animal group, and English mollusk followed the scientific Latin.
items.cn: 18、19 世纪动物学把 Mollusca 固定为一个主要动物类群，英语 mollusk 随科学拉丁语而定。

items.en: British usage prefers mollusc, American usage mollusk; both come from the same Latin adjective and neither is more original.
items.cn: 英式用法偏用 mollusc，美式用法偏用 mollusk；两者都出自同一个拉丁形容词，无所谓谁更原始。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root only): the Latin and French history is clear, but the pre-Latin root of mollis is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词根）：拉丁与法语阶段清楚，但 mollis 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式，并非有记录的形式。

note.en: Group one holds spellings and derivatives of the same word, plus one dangerous look-alike; group two holds shelled sea animals that are often confused with mollusks.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的拼写与派生形式，外加一个危险的形近词；第二组是常与软体动物混淆的带壳海生动物。

entries.definition: The same animal under the British spelling; the difference is orthographic, not biological.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个动物的英式拼写；差别在正字法，不在生物学。

entries.definition: The relational adjective 'of mollusks'; it cannot stand for the animal itself.
entries.definitionCN: 表关系的形容词「软体动物的」；它不能代替动物本身。

entries.definition: A substance that kills mollusks, built with -cide 'killing'; it is a chemical, not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 杀软体动物的药剂，由 -cide「杀」构成；它是化学品，不是动物。

entries.definition: From Latin mucus 'slime', not mollis 'soft'; the similar sound is accidental, and mucus is a secretion.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 mucus「黏液」，而非 mollis「柔软」；读音相近属偶然，mucus 是分泌物。

entries.definition: A market and fisheries word for edible mollusks and crustaceans together, so it is broader and less precise.
entries.definitionCN: 市场与渔业用语，兼指可食的软体动物与甲壳动物，因此更宽泛、更不精确。

entries.definition: A mollusk with two hinged shells, such as a clam or oyster; it is one class within the mollusks.
entries.definitionCN: 有两片铰合壳的软体动物，如蛤或牡蛎；它是软体动物中的一个纲。

entries.definition: A mollusk that moves on a muscular foot, such as a snail or slug; the name means 'stomach-foot'.
entries.definitionCN: 靠肌肉质足移动的软体动物，如螺或蛞蝓；名字意为「腹足」。

entries.definition: A mollusk with arms around the head, such as a squid or octopus; the name means 'head-foot'.
entries.definitionCN: 头部环生腕足的软体动物，如鱿鱼或章鱼；名字意为「头足」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root moll- means 'soft': a mollusk is the soft-bodied animal, shell or no shell.
normal.cn: 词根 moll- 意为「柔软」：软体动物就是身体柔软，有没有壳都一样。

normal.en: British mollusc and American mollusk are the same word in two spellings.
normal.cn: 英式 mollusc 与美式 mollusk 是同一个词的两种拼写。

normal.en: Bivalve, gastropod and cephalopod are the three mollusk classes most people meet.
normal.cn: 双壳类、腹足类、头足类是普通人最常遇到的三类软体动物。

normal.en: Shellfish is the market word; mollusk is the biological one.
normal.cn: shellfish 是市场用语；mollusk 是生物学用语。

normal.en: Molluscicide kills mollusks the way insecticide kills insects.
normal.cn: molluscicide 杀软体动物，正如 insecticide 杀虫。

abstract.en: Picture a soft body carrying its own house on its back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个柔软的身体把自家的房子背在背上。

abstract.en: Picture a shell on a beach as the only letter left by a writer.
abstract.cn: 想象海滩上一枚贝壳，是作者留下的唯一一封信。

abstract.en: Picture a squid nerve so thick that it made an entire science possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一根粗到足以让一整门科学成为可能的鱿鱼神经。

examples.en: The reef supports mollusks, crustaceans and many kinds of fish.
examples.cn: 这片礁养活软体动物、甲壳动物和许多种鱼。

examples.en: A single mollusk can filter several litres of water a day.
examples.cn: 一只软体动物一天能滤过好几升水。

examples.en: The fossil mollusks show that the basin was once under warm sea.
examples.cn: 软体动物化石表明这个盆地曾位于温暖的海洋之下。

dict_mnemonic.text: mollusk 读起来像「摸了个壳」——伸手一摸，摸到个软乎乎的带壳动物，就是软体动物

root: 拉丁 mollis「柔软」→ molluscus「柔软的、软壳的」→ 法语 mollusque；更早的印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a soft body into different roles: a phylum member, a food, a shell-maker, a garden pest, a fossil clock, a parasite host, a laboratory model and a farmed or invading species.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个柔软的身体进入不同角色：门类成员、食物、造壳者、园圃害虫、化石时钟、寄生虫宿主、实验模式动物，以及养殖或入侵的物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft body under a hard spiral shell, wet rock beneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬螺旋壳下的一团软身体，下面是湿岩。

branches.en: BODY AND HOUSE: the soft animal builds and carries a hard shell.
branches.cn: 身体与房子：柔软的身体造出并背着硬壳。

branches.en: FOOD: fisheries turn the animal into a market category.
branches.cn: 食物：渔业把这种动物变成市场类别。

branches.en: LAND PEST: the same phylum includes slugs in the garden.
branches.cn: 陆上害虫：同一门类也包括园子里的蛞蝓。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: shell chemistry makes the fossil a dating tool.
branches.cn: 深时：壳的化学成分使化石成为定年工具。

branches.en: USES BY OTHERS: a worm's host, a neuroscientist's model, a farmer's stock.
branches.cn: 被他人利用：寄生虫的宿主、神经科学家的模型、养殖者的存栏。

intro.en: Mollusk is a borrowed scientific noun; its English family is built with -an, -cide and compounds rather than with prefixes.
intro.cn: mollusk 是借入的科学名词；其英语词族靠 -an、-cide 与复合构成，而非加前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin mollis 'soft' gives molluscus and the scientific group name Mollusca; French mollusque is the direct source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mollis「柔软」衍生 molluscus 与科学类群名 Mollusca；法语 mollusque 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The root explains why a hard shell still hides a soft animal.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根解释了为何硬壳里仍是软身体。

items.example: The ending came into English with the French noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾随法语名词一起进入英语。

items.example: A mollusk crept over the rock.
items.exampleCN: 一只软体动物爬过岩石。

items.example: Mollusks dominate the shell hash on this beach.
items.exampleCN: 这片海滩的贝壳碎屑以软体动物为主。

items.example: The suffix makes the relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表关系的形容词。

items.example: The molluscan shell grew in yearly bands.
items.exampleCN: 软体动物的壳按年轮生长。

items.example: The pond was treated with a molluscicide before the snails were counted.
items.exampleCN: 在统计螺类数量之前，池塘先用了杀软体动物剂。

items.example: British textbooks write mollusc.
items.exampleCN: 英国教材写作 mollusc。

definition_zh: 软体动物的；软体动物似的；（旧义）柔软的
definition_en: relating to or characteristic of mollusks, or, in older use, soft and pliant
core_image: 显微镜下一片贝壳的横截面，一条条生长纹像树的年轮一样排开
scene: 实验室里，研究人员把一片贝壳切成薄片放在镜下，逐条记录它的生长纹。 The molluscan shell showed one growth band for each year of the animal's life.
sceneCN: 这里 molluscan 指「软体动物的」（第 1 个义项：与软体动物相关的）；句意为这片软体动物的贝壳每条生长带对应动物生命中的一年。

pos.zh: 软体动物的；软体动物特征的

derivatives.zh: 软体动物的（molluscan 的异体拼写）
柔软的；软体动物似的（旧用法）

senses.title: Relating to mollusks
senses.definition: of, relating to, or belonging to the mollusks
senses.definitionCN: 属于、关于或与软体动物有关的
senses.example: The molluscan shell showed one growth band per year.
senses.exampleCN: 这片软体动物的贝壳每年长出一条生长带。
senses.why: The suffix -an turns the noun mollusk into a relational adjective, so it answers 'of what kind?' rather than naming an animal.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -an 把名词 mollusk 变成表关系的形容词，因此它回答「属于哪一类」，而不是指某个动物。

senses.title: Characteristic of mollusk anatomy
senses.titleCN: 具有软体动物解剖特征的
senses.definition: showing the typical mollusk body plan of soft tissue, mantle and muscular foot
senses.definitionCN: 呈现软体动物典型的身体结构：软组织、外套膜与肌肉质足
senses.example: The molluscan body plan repeats in snails, clams and squid.
senses.exampleCN: 软体动物的身体结构在螺、蛤与鱿鱼中反复出现。
senses.why: Comparative anatomy uses the adjective to describe a shared architecture rather than a single species.
senses.whyCN: 比较解剖学用这个形容词描述共同的架构，而非某一个物种。

senses.title: Made of mollusk shell material
senses.titleCN: 由软体动物贝壳物质构成的
senses.definition: formed from the calcium carbonate of mollusk shells, as some sands and limestones are
senses.definitionCN: 由软体动物贝壳的碳酸钙形成，如某些砂与石灰岩
senses.example: The beach sand is largely molluscan debris.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海滩的沙主要是软体动物碎屑。
senses.why: Geology extends 'of mollusks' to 'made of their remains', because the shell is the durable part.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把「软体动物的」扩展为「由其遗骸构成的」，因为壳才是耐久的部分。

senses.title: Describing a fossil assemblage
senses.definition: used of a fossil fauna dominated by shells of ancient mollusks
senses.definitionCN: 用于指以古代软体动物贝壳为主的化石动物群
senses.example: The molluscan fauna places the bed in the Jurassic.
senses.exampleCN: 这套软体动物动物群把这层岩归入侏罗纪。
senses.why: Palaeontology names an assemblage by its commonest fossils, and mollusks often dominate.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学用最常见的化石来命名组合，而软体动物常占多数。

senses.title: Serving as a parasite host
senses.definition: describing a snail or other mollusk in whose body a parasite develops
senses.definitionCN: 描述寄生虫在其体内发育的螺或其他软体动物
senses.example: The molluscan host releases the next stage of the worm.
senses.exampleCN: 软体动物宿主释放出寄生虫的下一阶段。
senses.why: Parasitology needs a precise adjective because the host is an animal group, not one named species.
senses.whyCN: 寄生虫学需要精确的形容词，因为宿主是一个动物类群，而非某一个命名物种。

senses.title: Belonging to shellfish farming
senses.definition: used in fisheries for cultivated mollusks such as oysters, mussels and clams
senses.definitionCN: 渔业中用于指养殖的牡蛎、贻贝、蛤等软体动物
senses.example: Molluscan shellfish are grown on ropes and in trays.
senses.exampleCN: 贝类养殖品挂在绳上或放在托盘里生长。
senses.why: Industry adopts the adjective to distinguish mollusk products from crustacean ones.
senses.whyCN: 产业采用这个形容词，以把软体动物产品与甲壳动物产品区分开。

senses.title: Of the taxonomic group
senses.titleCN: 属于软体动物分类群的
senses.definition: belonging to the phylum Mollusca as a formal taxonomic unit
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为正式分类单元的软体动物门
senses.example: Molluscan affinities were confirmed by DNA.
senses.exampleCN: 软体动物的亲缘关系通过脱氧核糖核酸得到确认。
senses.why: Taxonomy uses the adjective for group membership, where the noun would wrongly suggest one animal.
senses.whyCN: 分类学用形容词表示类群归属，用名词则会误指某一个动物。

senses.title: Old sense: soft and pliant
senses.definition: in older medical and literary use, soft or yielding to the touch
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的医学与文学用法中，指触感柔软、易变形的
senses.example: The old herbals described a molluscan swelling of the flesh.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的本草书把这种肉组织的柔软肿胀称为 molluscan。
senses.why: The Latin adjective meant 'soft' before zoology narrowed it to a group of animals.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词先有「柔软」义，后来动物学才把它收窄为某一动物类群。

intro.en: Molluscan is Latin molluscus 'soft' plus the relational suffix -an; zoology fixed its modern meaning in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: molluscan 由拉丁 molluscus「柔软」加表关系的后缀 -an 构成；动物学在 19 世纪固定了它的现代义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Molluscus meant 'soft, soft-shelled', an adjective from mollis 'soft'. It described texture before it named a zoological group.
items.cn: molluscus 意为「柔软的、软壳的」，由 mollis「柔软」构成的形容词；它先描述质地，后才命名动物类群。

items.en: The suffix -anus formed adjectives of belonging, as in Romanus 'of Rome'; English -an continues it through French.
items.cn: 后缀 -anus 构成表归属的形容词，如 Romanus「罗马的」；英语 -an 经法语延续了它。

items.en: French naturalists used mollusque as a noun, and the adjective mollusque preceded English molluscan.
items.cn: 法国博物学家用 mollusque 作名词，其形容词形式先于英语 molluscan 出现。

items.en: English molluscan is recorded from the early nineteenth century in conchology and palaeontology, where shell collections needed a group adjective.
items.cn: 英语 molluscan 自 19 世纪初有记录，见于贝类学与古生物学，因为贝壳收藏需要一个类群形容词。

items.en: Molluscan and molluskan both occur; the k spelling matches American mollusk, the c spelling matches British mollusc.
items.cn: molluscan 与 molluskan 都有人用；k 拼写对应美式 mollusk，c 拼写对应英式 mollusc。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root only): mollis has no agreed pre-Latin etymology, so its Indo-European ancestry is a reconstruction, not a recorded derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词根）：mollis 没有公认的拉丁语之前词源，其印欧来源属重构，而非有记录的派生。

note.en: Group one holds spellings and derivatives that differ only in form; group two holds adjectives for related animal groups that cannot substitute for molluscan.
note.cn: 第一组是仅在形式上不同的拼写与派生词；第二组是相邻动物类群的形容词，不能替代 molluscan。

entries.definition: The same adjective with k, matching the American noun mollusk; the meaning does not change.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个形容词的 k 拼写，与美式名词 mollusk 一致；意义不变。

entries.definition: The animal itself; molluscan is only the adjective and cannot serve as the subject of a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 动物本身；molluscan 只是形容词，不能作句子主语。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning soft or mollusk-like; unlike molluscan, it is not a standard group term in zoology.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词，意为柔软的或似软体动物的；与 molluscan 不同，它不是动物学的标准类群术语。

entries.definition: A mollusk-killing substance; the ending -cide marks a pesticide, not an adjective of relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 杀软体动物的药剂；词尾 -cide 标示杀虫剂，而非表关系的形容词。

entries.definition: Of snails and slugs, one class of mollusks; it is narrower than molluscan.
entries.definitionCN: 指螺与蛞蝓，是软体动物中的一个纲；比 molluscan 窄。

entries.definition: Of clams and oysters, another mollusk class; again narrower than the whole phylum.
entries.definitionCN: 指蛤与牡蛎，是另一个软体动物纲；同样比整个门窄。

entries.definition: Of crabs, shrimp and barnacles, which are arthropods with a crust, not mollusks.
entries.definitionCN: 指蟹、虾、藤壶，它们是有硬壳的节肢动物，不是软体动物。

entries.definition: A food trade word covering mollusks and crustaceans together, so it crosses the biological divide.
entries.definitionCN: 食品行业用语，兼指软体动物与甲壳动物，因此跨越了生物分类界线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mollusk + -an: the -an makes it an adjective of belonging.
normal.cn: mollusk + -an：-an 使它成为表归属的形容词。

normal.en: Molluscan fauna, molluscan shell and molluscan host are the three common technical phrases.
normal.cn: molluscan fauna、molluscan shell、molluscan host 是三个常见技术搭配。

normal.en: The k spelling matches American mollusk; the c spelling matches British mollusc.
normal.cn: k 拼写对应美式 mollusk；c 拼写对应英式 mollusc。

normal.en: A crustacean is not molluscan: crabs and shrimp are arthropods.
normal.cn: 甲壳动物不属于软体动物：蟹和虾是节肢动物。

normal.en: The old sense 'soft' survives in medical writing, where the group meaning would make no sense.
normal.cn: 旧的「柔软」义仍见于医学文字，那里用类群义讲不通。

abstract.en: Picture a shell cut so thin that its year lines become a calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象贝壳被切得极薄，年轮成了日历。

abstract.en: Picture a whole phylum reduced to one adjective in front of the word shell.
abstract.cn: 想象整个门被压缩成 shell 前的一个形容词。

abstract.en: Picture soft flesh remembered long after the hard shell has become stone.
abstract.cn: 想象硬壳已成石头，软肉却仍被记得。

examples.en: Molluscan fossils are abundant in the shallow-water limestone.
examples.cn: 浅水石灰岩中富含软体动物化石。

examples.en: The parasite needs a molluscan host to complete its cycle.
examples.cn: 这种寄生虫需要一个软体动物宿主才能完成生活史。

examples.en: Molluscan shellfish are monitored for toxins each week.
examples.cn: 贝类海产每周都接受毒素监测。

dict_mnemonic.text: mollusk（软体动物）+ an（的）——软体动物的；看到 shell 前的 molluscan 就想「这是软体动物的壳」

root: 拉丁 molluscus「柔软的」+ 后缀 -an（拉丁 -anus「属于」）；mollis 在拉丁语之前的词源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses turn one group name into an adjective: relation, body plan, shell material, fossil fauna, parasite host, shellfish farming, taxonomy, and the older sense 'soft'.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把一个类群名变成形容词：关系、身体结构、贝壳材料、化石动物群、寄生虫宿主、贝类养殖、分类归属，以及较早的「柔软」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin shell section under a lens, its growth lines laid out like a calendar.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜下的一片薄壳截面，生长线像日历一样排开。

branches.en: GROUP MEMBERSHIP: the adjective marks belonging, whether in a lab or a taxonomic key.
branches.cn: 类群归属：无论实验室还是分类检索表，形容词都标记归属。

branches.en: SHARED ARCHITECTURE: mantle, soft tissue and muscular foot recur across the group.
branches.cn: 共同架构：外套膜、软组织与肌肉质足在类群内反复出现。

branches.en: HARD REMAINS: shells become sand, limestone and datable fossil assemblages.
branches.cn: 坚硬遗存：贝壳变成沙、石灰岩与可定年的化石组合。

branches.en: OTHER USES: a worm's host and a farmer's crop.
branches.cn: 其他用途：蠕虫的宿主与养殖者的作物。

branches.en: OLDER TEXTURE: 'soft' survives where the group meaning does not fit.
branches.cn: 更早的质地义：在类群义不适用处，「柔软」仍活着。

intro.en: Molluscan is a transparent derivative: a borrowed stem plus one Latin suffix, with a spelling variant for each national norm.
intro.cn: molluscan 是透明的派生词：借入词干加一个拉丁后缀，并按各国规范有两种拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin mollis 'soft' yields molluscus; the suffix -anus yields English -an. The same stem gives mollusk, mollusc and Mollusca.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mollis「柔软」衍生 molluscus；后缀 -anus 对应英语 -an。同一词干还给出 mollusk、mollusc 与 Mollusca。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of softness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着「柔软」的意思。

items.example: The suffix makes a group adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成类群形容词。

items.example: The molluscan shell grew in bands.
items.exampleCN: 软体动物的壳按带生长。

items.example: Some journals print molluskan.
items.exampleCN: 有些期刊印作 molluskan。

items.example: A mollusk built the shell.
items.exampleCN: 一只软体动物造出了这枚壳。

items.example: British texts prefer mollusc.
items.exampleCN: 英国文本偏用 mollusc。

items.example: The older adjective described soft tissue.
items.exampleCN: 这个较旧的形容词描述柔软组织。

items.meaning: the mollusk species of a place or layer
items.meaningCN: 某地或某层的软体动物群
items.example: The molluscan fauna dates the bed.
items.exampleCN: 软体动物群为这层岩定年。

definition_zh: 甲壳动物（虾、蟹、藤壶等有硬壳的节肢动物）
definition_en: an arthropod with a hard shell, such as a crab, shrimp, lobster or barnacle
core_image: 潮池石缝里一只螃蟹举起硬壳钳子，壳面反着水光
scene: 潮池里，一只小蟹横着快跑，硬壳在浅水中反着光。 A small crustacean scuttled sideways through the pool, its hard shell glinting under the water.
sceneCN: 这里 crustacean 指「甲壳动物」（第 1 个义项：有硬壳的节肢动物）；句意为一只小甲壳动物横着穿过潮池，硬壳在水下反光。

forms.label: 形容词（有壳的；甲壳类的）

derivatives.zh: 十足目动物（蟹、虾等甲壳动物）

senses.title: A member of the group Crustacea
senses.definition: any arthropod of the group Crustacea, with a hard exoskeleton and usually two pairs of antennae
senses.definitionCN: 甲壳动物类群中任何有硬外骨骼、通常有两对触角的节肢动物
senses.example: A small crustacean scuttled sideways through the pool.
senses.exampleCN: 一只小甲壳动物横着穿过潮池。
senses.why: The name comes from Latin crusta 'shell', because the group is defined by its hard casing.
senses.whyCN: 名字来自拉丁 crusta「硬壳」，因为这一类群正是以硬壳为标志。

senses.title: The group as a whole
