senses.definition: the crustaceans collectively, treated as one large subgroup of arthropods
senses.definitionCN: 把所有甲壳动物作为一个大的节肢动物亚群来看
senses.example: Crustaceans dominate the tide pool at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里潮池由甲壳类占据主导。
senses.why: Collective use lets the plural stand for the group without naming each species.
senses.whyCN: 集合用法让复数形式代表整个类群，无需逐一命名物种。

senses.title: An edible crustacean
senses.definition: a crab, shrimp, lobster or similar animal harvested for food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物捕捞的蟹、虾、龙虾或类似动物
senses.example: The restaurant buys crustaceans from the local boats.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅从本地渔船购买甲壳类。
senses.why: Fisheries use the group name for the catch, so it doubles as a menu category.
senses.whyCN: 渔业用类群名指渔获，因此它同时成了菜单类别。

senses.title: The hard shell itself
senses.definition: the chitinous exoskeleton that a crustacean sheds as it grows
senses.definitionCN: 甲壳动物生长时蜕去的几丁质外骨骼
senses.example: The crustacean shell left behind was perfectly intact.
senses.exampleCN: 留下的甲壳完好无损。
senses.why: The shell is shed whole, so the word can name the casing apart from the animal.
senses.whyCN: 壳是整片蜕下的，因此这个词也能指脱离动物体的外壳。

senses.title: A fossil crustacean
senses.definition: ancient crustacean remains, common as microfossils in marine rocks
senses.definitionCN: 古代甲壳动物的遗骸，常以微体化石形式存在于海相岩石中
senses.example: Ostracods are tiny crustaceans used to date the core.
senses.exampleCN: 介形虫是微小的甲壳动物，用来给岩芯定年。
senses.why: Their shed shells fossilize well, which makes the group a geological tool.
senses.whyCN: 它们蜕下的壳容易形成化石，使这一类群成了地质工具。

senses.title: A parasitic crustacean
senses.definition: a crustacean that lives on or in another animal, such as a sea louse on a fish
senses.definitionCN: 附着在另一动物体表或体内生活的甲壳动物，如鱼身上的海虱
senses.example: Sea lice are crustaceans that damage farmed salmon.
senses.exampleCN: 海虱是危害养殖鲑鱼的甲壳动物。
senses.why: Parasitism evolved repeatedly in the group, so the word covers very different life habits.
senses.whyCN: 寄生在类群内多次演化出现，因此这个词涵盖差异极大的生活方式。

senses.title: A laboratory model
senses.definition: a crustacean used in research, such as Daphnia in toxicity tests
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究的甲壳动物，如毒性测试中的水蚤
senses.example: Daphnia is a crustacean used in standard toxicity tests.
senses.exampleCN: 水蚤是标准毒性测试中使用的一种甲壳动物。
senses.why: Short life cycles and sensitivity to chemicals make some crustaceans ideal test animals.
senses.whyCN: 生活史短、对化学品敏感，使某些甲壳动物成为理想的试验动物。

senses.title: A farmed crop
senses.definition: a crustacean raised in ponds or tanks for food
senses.definitionCN: 在池塘或水箱中为食用而养殖的甲壳动物
senses.example: Shrimp are the most valuable crustaceans in aquaculture.
senses.exampleCN: 虾是水产养殖中价值最高的甲壳类。
senses.why: Farming turns the animal into a commodity, and the group name becomes an industry label.
senses.whyCN: 养殖把动物变成商品，类群名也成了行业标签。

intro.en: Crustacean is built on Latin crusta 'crust, shell' plus the adjective ending -aceus, and entered English through scientific Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: crustacean 由拉丁 crusta「硬壳、外壳」加形容词词尾 -aceus 构成，经科学拉丁语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Crusta meant 'crust, rind, shell', the hard outer layer of bread or of an animal. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: crusta 意为「硬壳、外皮、外壳」，指面包或动物体表的硬层。其更深来源未有定论。

items.en: The adjective crustaceus 'having a crust or shell' was used for animals with hard coverings, not only for crabs.
items.cn: 形容词 crustaceus「有壳的」用于带硬覆盖的动物，并不只指蟹。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century zoology raised Crustacea to a formal group name, separating crabs, shrimp and barnacles from insects.
items.cn: 18、19 世纪动物学把 Crustacea 提升为正式类群名，把蟹、虾、藤壶与昆虫分开。

items.en: English crustacean appears in the nineteenth century as the noun for a member of that group, alongside the older adjective crustaceous.
items.cn: 英语 crustacean 在 19 世纪作为该类群成员的名称出现，与更早的形容词 crustaceous 并存。

items.en: As seafood industries grew, crustacean became the neutral word for crabs and shrimp on menus and in regulations.
items.cn: 随着海产行业发展，crustacean 成了菜单与法规中对蟹、虾的中性称谓。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): crusta has no agreed etymology, so any pre-Latin form proposed for it is a reconstruction, not a documented word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：crusta 没有公认词源，凡为其提出的拉丁语之前形式都属重构，而非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds crust- words that look close but name shells, rocks or a geological period; group two holds animal-group words easily confused with crustacean.
note.cn: 第一组是同含 crust- 但指外壳、地壳或地质年代的形近词；第二组是易与甲壳动物混淆的动物类群词。

entries.definition: The hard outer layer of bread or rock; it is the source noun, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 面包或岩石的硬外层；它是来源名词，不是动物。

entries.definition: Meaning 'having a crust'; it describes the shell but does not name a crab or shrimp.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「有硬壳的」；它描述外壳，却不指蟹或虾。

entries.definition: Relating to the crust of the Earth; the same noun, an entirely different field.
entries.definitionCN: 与地壳有关的；同出一个名词，却属完全不同的领域。

entries.definition: The geological period named from Latin creta 'chalk', not crusta; the similar ending is a false friend.
entries.definitionCN: 地质年代名，来自拉丁 creta「白垩」，而非 crusta；词尾相似是假朋友。

entries.definition: Any jointed-legged invertebrate with an exoskeleton; crustaceans are one branch of the arthropods.
entries.definitionCN: 任何有外骨骼、具分节附肢的无脊椎动物；甲壳动物是节肢动物的一个分支。

entries.definition: A market term for edible crustaceans and mollusks together, broader and looser than crustacean.
entries.definitionCN: 市场用语，兼指可食甲壳动物与软体动物，比 crustacean 更宽泛、更松散。

entries.definition: A crustacean with ten legs, such as a crab or lobster; it is a subgroup, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 有十条腿的甲壳动物，如蟹或龙虾；它是亚群，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A crustacean that cements itself to rocks or hulls; it is a crustacean even though it looks like a shell.
entries.definitionCN: 把自己黏在岩石或船体上的甲壳动物；虽像贝壳，它仍是甲壳动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: crust- means 'shell': a crustacean is the shelled animal.
normal.cn: crust- 意为「壳」：甲壳动物就是带壳的动物。

normal.en: Crabs, shrimp, lobsters and barnacles are all crustaceans, though they look very different.
normal.cn: 蟹、虾、龙虾、藤壶都是甲壳动物，尽管外形差异很大。

normal.en: A crustacean is an arthropod, but not every arthropod is a crustacean: insects and spiders are outside the group.
normal.cn: 甲壳动物是节肢动物，但并非所有节肢动物都是甲壳动物：昆虫与蜘蛛不在其中。

normal.en: Shellfish is the menu word; crustacean is the biological one.
normal.cn: shellfish 是菜单用语；crustacean 是生物学用语。

normal.en: Decapods are the ten-legged crustaceans, the ones most often eaten.
normal.cn: 十足目是有十条腿的甲壳动物，也是最常被食用的一类。

abstract.en: Picture an animal wearing its skeleton on the outside and shedding it to grow.
abstract.cn: 想象一个把骨骼穿在外面的动物，靠蜕掉它来长大。

abstract.en: Picture a barnacle that looks like a shell but is actually a shrimp glued down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只藤壶，看起来像贝壳，其实是一只黏住的虾。

abstract.en: Picture a microfossil the size of a pinhead dating a whole rock layer.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚针头大小的微体化石，为整层岩石定年。

examples.en: Crustaceans shed their shells several times before they reach adult size.
examples.cn: 甲壳动物在长到成体大小之前要蜕壳好几次。

examples.en: The trap caught crustaceans but no fish.
examples.cn: 这个陷阱只捕到甲壳类，没有鱼。

examples.en: Ocean acidification makes it harder for crustaceans to build their shells.
examples.cn: 海洋酸化使甲壳动物更难构建外壳。

dict_mnemonic.text: crust（硬壳）+ acean——带硬壳的一大类，就是甲壳动物；记「蟹虾都穿硬壳」

root: 拉丁 crusta「硬壳、外皮」→ crustaceus「有壳的」→ 近代拉丁 Crustacea；crusta 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a shelled animal through its roles: group member, collective group, seafood, shed shell, fossil, parasite, lab model and farmed crop.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个带壳动物穿过各种角色：类群成员、整体类群、海产食物、蜕下的壳、化石、寄生虫、实验模型与养殖对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crab in a tide pool, its hard shell reflecting the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：潮池里的一只蟹，硬壳映着水光。

branches.en: ONE AND MANY: a single shelled animal, or the whole group treated as a unit.
branches.cn: 个体与整体：单个带壳动物，或把整个类群当作一个单位。

branches.en: COMMODITY: the same animal appears on a menu and in a farm pond.
branches.cn: 商品：同一种动物既出现在菜单上，也出现在养殖池里。

branches.en: THE CAST-OFF: the shell can be named apart from the living animal.
branches.cn: 蜕下之物：壳可以脱离活体单独被指称。

branches.en: EVIDENCE AND EXPERIMENT: shed shells become fossils; small species become test subjects.
branches.cn: 证据与实验：蜕壳变成化石；小型种类成为试验对象。

branches.en: THE OTHER LIFESTYLE: some crustaceans live on other animals.
branches.cn: 另一种活法：有些甲壳动物寄居在其他动物身上。

intro.en: Crustacean is a Latin-derived noun plus the English suffix -an; the stem is the same one that gives crust and crustal.
intro.cn: crustacean 是拉丁语源名词加英语后缀 -an；词干与 crust、crustal 相同。

latinIntro.en: Latin crusta gives crust, crustaceus and crustulum; crustaceus plus the group name Crustacea produced the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crusta 衍生 crust、crustaceus 与 crustulum；crustaceus 加类群名 Crustacea 产生了英语名词。

items.example: The root supplies the shell image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「壳」的形象。

items.example: Crustaceus means shell-covered.
items.exampleCN: crustaceus 意为覆有硬壳的。

items.example: A crustacean scuttled across the pool.
items.exampleCN: 一只甲壳动物横穿潮池。

items.example: Crustaceans crowded the bait.
items.exampleCN: 甲壳动物挤满了饵料。

items.example: The crustaceous covering protects the body.
items.exampleCN: 硬壳覆盖保护着身体。

items.example: The crust cracked under the tide.
items.exampleCN: 硬壳在潮水下裂开。

items.example: Crustal movement raised the coast.
items.exampleCN: 地壳运动抬高了海岸。

items.example: Crustacea is a large subphylum.
items.exampleCN: 甲壳类是一个很大的亚门。

definition_zh: 节肢动物（身体分节、具外骨骼与分节附肢的无脊椎动物）
definition_en: an invertebrate with a segmented body, a hard exoskeleton and jointed legs, such as an insect, spider or crab
core_image: 放大镜下一条分节的腿正在弯折，每个关节都像小小的折页铰链
scene: 放大镜下，观察者看见一条分节的腿在弯折，每一节都像小小的铰链。 The arthropod moved its segmented leg at each joint like a tiny hinge.
sceneCN: 这里 arthropod 指「节肢动物」（第 1 个义项：身体分节、具外骨骼与分节附肢的动物）；句意为这只节肢动物让分节的腿在每个关节处像小铰链一样转动。

forms.label: 复合形容词（节肢动物传播的）

senses.title: A member of the phylum Arthropoda
senses.definition: any invertebrate of the phylum Arthropoda, with a segmented body and jointed appendages
senses.definitionCN: 节肢动物门中任何身体分节、附肢也分节的无脊椎动物
senses.example: The arthropod moved its segmented leg at each joint.
senses.exampleCN: 这只节肢动物让分节的腿在每个关节处转动。
senses.why: The name is Greek for 'jointed foot', so the defining feature is written into the word itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字在希腊语里就是「分节的足」，因此定义特征直接写进了词里。

senses.title: The group as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的节肢动物类群
senses.definition: the arthropods collectively, the largest animal phylum
senses.definitionCN: 所有节肢动物作为一个整体，是动物界最大的门
senses.example: Arthropods make up most known animal species.
senses.exampleCN: 节肢动物构成了已知动物物种的大多数。
senses.why: Because the group is enormous, the plural often stands for a category rather than a set of individuals.
senses.whyCN: 由于类群极庞大，复数形式常代表一个范畴，而不是若干个体。

senses.title: Used as an attributive label
senses.titleCN: 作定语标示传播或来源
senses.definition: used before another noun to say that something is carried, caused or made by arthropods
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示由节肢动物携带、引起或制造
senses.example: Arthropod-borne viruses spread faster in warm, wet seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 节肢动物传播的病毒在温暖潮湿的季节扩散更快。
senses.why: Public health needed a compact label for diseases carried by insects and ticks, and arthropod supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生需要简洁标签来指昆虫与蜱类携带的疾病，arthropod 正好补上。

senses.title: A fossil arthropod
senses.definition: ancient arthropod remains, including trilobites and fossil insects
senses.definitionCN: 古代节肢动物遗骸，包括三叶虫与昆虫化石
senses.example: Trilobites are arthropods that vanished before the dinosaurs.
senses.exampleCN: 三叶虫是在恐龙之前就灭绝的节肢动物。
senses.why: The hard exoskeleton fossilizes well, making arthropods central to palaeontology.
senses.whyCN: 硬外骨骼容易形成化石，使节肢动物成为古生物学的核心对象。

senses.title: An agricultural pest
senses.definition: an arthropod that damages crops or stored food
senses.definitionCN: 损害作物或仓储食物的节肢动物
senses.example: The spray targets arthropods that feed on the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 这种喷剂针对取食叶片的节肢动物。
senses.why: Pest control needs a word broad enough to cover insects and mites together.
senses.whyCN: 害虫防治需要一个足够宽、能同时涵盖昆虫与螨类的词。

senses.title: A disease vector
senses.definition: an arthropod that transmits a pathogen from one host to another, such as a mosquito or tick
senses.definitionCN: 把病原体从一个宿主传给另一宿主的节肢动物，如蚊或蜱
senses.example: The mosquito is the arthropod responsible for the outbreak.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子是造成这次疫情的节肢动物媒介。
senses.why: Epidemiology uses the phylum name because the vector may be a fly, a flea or a tick.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学用门名，因为媒介可能是蝇、蚤或蜱。

senses.title: A laboratory model
senses.definition: an arthropod used in genetics or physiology, especially the fruit fly
senses.definitionCN: 用于遗传学或生理学研究的节肢动物，尤指果蝇
senses.example: The fruit fly gave arthropods a central place in genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 果蝇让节肢动物在遗传学中占据了中心位置。
senses.why: Short generations and easy breeding made one arthropod the workhorse of genetics.
senses.whyCN: 世代短、易饲养，使某一种节肢动物成了遗传学的主力。

senses.title: An introduced or invasive species
senses.titleCN: 引入或入侵的节肢动物
senses.definition: an arthropod that has spread outside its native range and disrupts ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 扩散到原分布区之外、扰乱生态系统的节肢动物
senses.example: The introduced arthropod has no local predator.
senses.exampleCN: 这种外来节肢动物在当地没有天敌。
senses.why: Invasion biology names the group because the invader is often an insect or a crab.
senses.whyCN: 入侵生物学用类群名，因为入侵者常是昆虫或蟹类。

intro.en: Arthropod is Greek arthron 'joint' plus pous 'foot', a scientific compound that says exactly what the animal is. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: arthropod 由希腊 arthron「关节」加 pous「足」构成，这个科学复合词把动物的特征直接说了出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arthron meant 'joint, articulation'. It is generally connected to a root meaning 'to fit together', but that earlier form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: arthron 意为「关节、接合处」。一般认为它与意为「接合在一起」的词根有关，但那个更早的形式属重构。

items.en: Pous (stem pod-) meant 'foot', the same word behind tripod and podiatry.
items.cn: pous（词干 pod-）意为「足」，tripod 与 podiatry 也出自这个词。

items.en: The compound 'jointed foot' was coined in modern scientific Latin as Arthropoda and then borrowed into English as arthropod.
items.cn: 「分节的足」这一复合形式在近代科学拉丁语中被造为 Arthropoda，随后作为 arthropod 借入英语。

items.en: Nineteenth-century zoology fixed Arthropoda as the phylum containing insects, arachnids and crustaceans; the exact coiner and date are not settled.
items.cn: 19 世纪动物学把 Arthropoda 固定为包含昆虫、蛛形类与甲壳类的门；确切的造词者与年代尚无定论。

items.en: Twentieth-century public health and agriculture produced fixed phrases such as arthropod vector and arthropod-borne disease.
items.cn: 20 世纪的公共卫生与农业产生了 arthropod vector、arthropod-borne disease 等固定说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (details only): the Greek roots are clear, but the pre-Greek root of arthron is reconstructed and the exact first use of the English noun is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅细节）：希腊词根清楚，但 arthron 在希腊语之前的词根属重构，英语名词的确切首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek joint-root; group two holds animal-group names that overlap with arthropods without being synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「关节」词根的字词；第二组是与节肢动物重叠但并非同义的动物类群名。

entries.definition: Inflammation of a joint, built from arthron 'joint' plus -itis 'inflammation'; same root, medical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 关节炎症，由 arthron「关节」加 -itis「炎症」构成；同词根，医学义。

entries.definition: A joint or a joint disorder, from the same Greek root; it names a body part, not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 指关节或关节病变，同出希腊词根；它指身体部位，不指动物。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning 'joint', used in arthroscopy and arthroplasty; it is a word part, not a whole word.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「关节」的构词成分，用于 arthroscopy、arthroplasty；它是词素，不是完整单词。

entries.definition: The formal Latin name of the phylum; Arthropoda is the group, arthropod is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 该门的正式拉丁名；Arthropoda 是类群，arthropod 是其中一个成员。

entries.definition: A six-legged arthropod with three body regions; insects are a class inside Arthropoda, not the whole phylum.
entries.definitionCN: 有六条腿、身体分三区的节肢动物；昆虫是节肢动物门内的一个纲，不是整个门。

entries.definition: An eight-legged arthropod such as a spider or tick; another class within the same phylum.
entries.definitionCN: 有八条腿的节肢动物，如蜘蛛或蜱；同一门内的另一个纲。

entries.definition: A shelled arthropod such as a crab; it is a major subgroup of arthropods.
entries.definitionCN: 有硬壳的节肢动物，如蟹；它是节肢动物的一个主要亚群。

entries.definition: Any animal without a backbone, including arthropods, mollusks and worms; it is broader than arthropod.
entries.definitionCN: 任何没有脊椎的动物，包括节肢动物、软体动物与蠕虫；比 arthropod 更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: arthro- 'joint' + pod 'foot': the animal with jointed feet.
normal.cn: arthro-「关节」+ pod「足」：长着分节足的动物。

normal.en: Insects, spiders, crabs and centipedes are all arthropods, but each is a different subgroup.
normal.cn: 昆虫、蜘蛛、蟹、蜈蚣都是节肢动物，但各属不同亚群。

normal.en: Arthropoda is the phylum; arthropod is one member of it.
normal.cn: Arthropoda 是门；arthropod 是门中的一个成员。

normal.en: Arthropod-borne disease is the fixed public-health phrase for infections carried by insects and ticks.
normal.cn: arthropod-borne disease 是公共卫生固定说法，指昆虫与蜱类携带的感染。

normal.en: The hard exoskeleton is why arthropods fossilize so well.
normal.cn: 硬外骨骼正是节肢动物容易形成化石的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a suit of armour worn outside the body, with every limb on a hinge.
abstract.cn: 想象一套穿在身体外面的盔甲，每条肢体都装在铰链上。

abstract.en: Picture a group so numerous that it outnumbers all other animals combined.
abstract.cn: 想象一个类群，数量超过其他所有动物的总和。

abstract.en: Picture a mosquito that is both a pest and a delivery route for disease.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蚊子，既是害虫，也是疾病的投送路径。

examples.en: Arthropods account for more than half of all described animal species.
examples.cn: 节肢动物占全部已描述动物物种的一半以上。

examples.en: The trap was designed to sample small arthropods in the soil.
examples.cn: 这个陷阱用来采集土壤中的小型节肢动物。

examples.en: Arthropod vectors include mosquitoes, fleas and ticks.
examples.cn: 节肢动物媒介包括蚊、蚤与蜱。

dict_mnemonic.text: arthro（关节）+ pod（足）——关节一节一节、足也一节一节，就是节肢动物

root: 希腊 arthron「关节」+ pous（词干 pod-）「足」；arthron 的更深词源一般认为是「接合」词根，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a jointed animal across disciplines: a phylum member, the vast group, a disease label, a fossil, a pest, a vector, a lab model and an invader.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一种分节动物穿过不同学科：门类成员、庞大类群、疾病标签、化石、害虫、传播媒介、实验模型与入侵者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a segmented leg bending at each joint like a row of tiny hinges.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条分节的腿在每个关节处弯折，像一排小铰链。

branches.en: ONE AND ALL: a single jointed animal, or the largest phylum on Earth.
branches.cn: 个体与全部：单个分节动物，或地球上最大的门。

branches.en: CARRIER: the same group name labels diseases and names the vector.
branches.cn: 携带者：同一类群名既给疾病贴标签，也指传播媒介。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: hard exoskeletons make excellent fossils.
branches.cn: 深时：硬外骨骼极易形成化石。

branches.en: TROUBLE: the group includes both native pests and introduced invaders.
branches.cn: 麻烦：类群中既有本地害虫，也有外来入侵者。

branches.en: RESEARCH: short generations make one arthropod a genetic workhorse.
branches.cn: 研究：世代短，使某种节肢动物成为遗传学主力。

intro.en: Arthropod is a transparent Greek compound, and both halves recur in medical and scientific words.
intro.cn: arthropod 是透明的希腊复合词，两半都反复出现在医学与科学词汇中。

latinIntro.en: The source is Greek, not Latin; arthron and pous entered scientific Latin as Arthropoda before English borrowed the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是希腊语而非拉丁语；arthron 与 pous 先进入科学拉丁语构成 Arthropoda，英语再借入该名词。

items.example: The prefix marks the jointed body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出分节的身体。

items.example: The second element marks the limbs.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分标出肢体。

items.example: Every arthropod has a segmented body.
items.exampleCN: 每只节肢动物都有分节的身体。

items.example: Arthropods fill every land habitat.
items.exampleCN: 节肢动物遍布每一处陆地生境。

items.example: The arthropodan cuticle is stiff but flexible.
items.exampleCN: 节肢动物的角质层坚硬而有韧性。

items.example: Arthropoda is the largest phylum.
items.exampleCN: 节肢动物门是最大的门。

items.example: Arthritis shares the joint root but names a disease.
items.exampleCN: arthritis 同出「关节」词根，却指一种疾病。

items.example: Tripod uses the same foot word.
items.exampleCN: tripod 用了同一个「足」词。

items.example: Arthropod-borne infections rise in summer.
items.exampleCN: 节肢动物传播的感染在夏季增多。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 具分节足的动物（节肢动物门）

definition_en: an animal without a backbone, or lacking a backbone
core_image: 退潮的水洼里，一团没有骨架的软体摊在石上，靠水支撑着形状
scene: 退潮后的水洼里，一只没有骨架的软体动物摊在石头上，靠残留的水维持形状。 Without a backbone, the invertebrate relied on the water to hold its shape.
sceneCN: 这里 invertebrate 指「无脊椎动物」（第 1 个义项：没有脊柱的动物）；句意为由于没有脊柱，这只无脊椎动物只能靠水来维持体形。

derivatives.zh: 无脊椎动物类群（旧分类名）

senses.title: An animal without a backbone
senses.definition: any animal that lacks a vertebral column, including insects, worms, mollusks and crustaceans
senses.definitionCN: 任何没有脊柱的动物，包括昆虫、蠕虫、软体动物与甲壳动物
senses.example: Without a backbone, the invertebrate relied on water to hold its shape.
senses.exampleCN: 由于没有脊柱，这只无脊椎动物靠水维持体形。
senses.why: The word is literally 'without vertebrae': in- 'not' plus vertebra, the bones of the spine.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面就是「没有脊椎」：in-「不」加 vertebra（脊柱的骨节）。

senses.title: The adjective: lacking a backbone
senses.definition: describing an animal or body plan that has no spinal column
senses.definitionCN: 描述没有脊柱的动物或身体结构
senses.example: The invertebrate body plan allows bending in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 无脊椎的身体结构允许向各个方向弯曲。
senses.why: English uses the same form for noun and adjective, so the ending -ate does double duty.
senses.whyCN: 英语中名词与形容词同形，因此 -ate 词尾同时承担两种功能。

senses.title: The field of invertebrate zoology
senses.titleCN: 无脊椎动物学这一学科
senses.definition: the branch of zoology that studies animals without backbones
senses.definitionCN: 研究无脊柱动物的动物学分支
senses.example: Invertebrate zoology covers far more species than vertebrate zoology.
senses.exampleCN: 无脊椎动物学涵盖的物种远多于脊椎动物学。
senses.why: Because most animal species lack a backbone, the adjective became a discipline label.
senses.whyCN: 由于大多数动物物种没有脊柱，这个形容词成了一个学科标签。

senses.title: A fossil invertebrate
senses.definition: ancient remains of an animal without a backbone, often shells or exoskeletons
senses.definitionCN: 无脊柱动物的古代遗骸，常为贝壳或外骨骼
senses.example: The oldest invertebrate fossils are more than half a billion years old.
senses.exampleCN: 最古老的无脊椎动物化石已有五亿多年历史。
senses.why: Hard shells and exoskeletons preserve far better than soft vertebrate tissue, so the fossil record is dominated by invertebrates.
senses.whyCN: 硬壳与外骨骼比脊椎动物的软组织更易保存，因此化石记录以无脊椎动物为主。

senses.title: A marine invertebrate
senses.definition: an invertebrate living in the sea, such as a coral, crab or sea worm
senses.definitionCN: 生活在海中的无脊椎动物，如珊瑚、蟹或海虫
senses.example: Marine invertebrates build most of the reef structure.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋无脊椎动物建造了大部分礁体结构。
senses.why: Ecology uses the category because reef builders and sea-floor communities cross many phyla.
senses.whyCN: 生态学使用这一范畴，因为造礁者与海底群落跨越许多门。

senses.title: A source of food and stock
senses.definition: an invertebrate harvested or farmed for food, such as shrimp, squid or oysters
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物捕捞或养殖的无脊椎动物，如虾、鱿鱼或牡蛎
senses.example: Most aquaculture production is invertebrate.
senses.exampleCN: 水产养殖的大部分产量来自无脊椎动物。
senses.why: The category groups together very different edible animals that share only the absence of a spine.
senses.whyCN: 这一范畴把差异极大、只共享「没有脊柱」这一点的可食动物归在一起。

senses.title: Figurative: lacking firmness or courage
senses.definition: describing a person or organization seen as weak-willed or lacking firm principles
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人或组织意志软弱、缺乏坚定原则
senses.example: Critics called the committee invertebrate for postponing the decision again.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说委员会又一次推迟决定，毫无骨气。
senses.why: The metaphor takes 'no backbone' from anatomy and applies it to character: no spine, no resolve.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把解剖上的「没有脊柱」用到性格上：没有脊梁，就没有决断。

senses.title: A bioindicator community
senses.definition: invertebrates used to assess water or soil quality because they respond quickly to pollution
senses.definitionCN: 因对污染反应迅速而被用来评估水或土壤质量的无脊椎动物
senses.example: Stream invertebrates are sampled to grade water quality.
senses.exampleCN: 通过采样溪流无脊椎动物来评定水质。
senses.why: Monitoring programs use the category because mayflies, snails and worms together signal different pollution levels.
senses.whyCN: 监测项目使用这一范畴，因为蜉蝣、螺与蠕虫共同指示不同的污染水平。

intro.en: Invertebrate is Latin in- 'not' plus vertebra 'joint of the spine', with the adjective ending -ate; the word is a modern scientific formation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: invertebrate 由拉丁 in-「不」加 vertebra「脊柱的骨节」，再加形容词词尾 -ate 构成；它是近代科学造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertebra meant a joint, especially a joint of the spine, from vertere 'to turn'. The link to 'turn' is generally accepted; the deeper root is reconstructed.
items.cn: vertebra 意为「关节」，尤指脊柱的关节，来自 vertere「转动」。与「转动」的联系一般被接受；更深的词根属重构。

items.en: The prefix in- 'not' negates the noun, so an invertebrate is literally 'one without vertebrae'.
items.cn: 前缀 in-「不」否定该名词，因此 invertebrate 字面就是「没有脊椎的东西」。

items.en: Lamarck's early nineteenth-century classification used invertébrés for animals without a spinal column, and English borrowed the term.
items.cn: 拉马克在 19 世纪初的分类中使用 invertébrés 指没有脊柱的动物，英语借入了这个词。

items.en: English invertebrate appears in the nineteenth century as both noun and adjective, in zoology and in general prose.
items.cn: 英语 invertebrate 在 19 世纪出现，既作名词也作形容词，见于动物学与一般散文。

items.en: By the later nineteenth century 'no backbone' was applied to people and institutions lacking firmness, and the figurative sense entered dictionaries.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪后期，「没有脊梁」被用于形容缺乏坚定性的人与机构，比喻义进入词典。

items.en: Source uncertain (details only): the Latin stages are clear, but the pre-Latin root of vertere is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅细节）：拉丁阶段清楚，但 vertere 的拉丁语之前词根属重构，英语确切首见书证也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same vertebra stock that are easily confused; group two holds animal-category words that overlap with invertebrate.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 vertebra 词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是与无脊椎动物重叠的动物范畴词。

entries.definition: An animal with a backbone; it differs from invertebrate by the single negative prefix in-.
entries.definitionCN: 有脊柱的动物；与 invertebrate 只差一个否定前缀 in-。

entries.definition: A single bone of the spine; several are vertebrae. The animal word is built on this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 脊柱的一块骨；多块为 vertebrae。动物词正是在这个名词上构成的。

entries.definition: Relating to a vertebra or the spine, as in vertebral column; it is not the animal category word.
entries.definitionCN: 与椎骨或脊柱有关，如 vertebral column；它不是动物类别词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to turn upside down, from in- + vertere 'turn'; it shares the root but is not related in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为翻转，由 in- + vertere「转」构成；同词根，但意义无关。

entries.definition: A jointed-legged invertebrate; arthropods are the largest subgroup of invertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: 具分节附肢的无脊椎动物；节肢动物是最大的无脊椎动物亚群。

entries.definition: A soft-bodied invertebrate, usually with a shell; another subgroup, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 身体柔软、通常带壳的无脊椎动物；另一个亚群，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A segmented worm such as an earthworm; it is one kind of invertebrate among very many.
entries.definitionCN: 分节的蠕虫，如蚯蚓；它是众多无脊椎动物中的一类。

entries.definition: Small drifting animals in water, many of them invertebrates; the term names a lifestyle, not a category.
entries.definitionCN: 水中漂浮的小型动物，许多是无脊椎动物；这个词命名生活方式，而不是类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'not' + vertebrate 'backboned': the animal with no spine.
normal.cn: in-「不」+ vertebrate「有脊椎的」：没有脊柱的动物。

normal.en: Vertebra is one spinal bone; vertebrae are several; invertebrate means none at all.
normal.cn: vertebra 是一块椎骨，vertebrae 是多块，invertebrate 则一块也没有。

normal.en: Most animal species are invertebrates: insects alone outnumber all vertebrates.
normal.cn: 大多数动物物种是无脊椎动物：仅昆虫就超过所有脊椎动物。

normal.en: The figurative use is 'no backbone' in character, not in anatomy.
normal.cn: 比喻义指性格上「没有脊梁」，而非解剖结构。

normal.en: Invertebrate zoology is a field name, because the category covers dozens of phyla.
normal.cn: invertebrate zoology 是学科名，因为这一范畴涵盖数十个门。

abstract.en: Picture a body that holds itself up with water instead of bone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用水的力量而不是骨头来支撑的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a committee with no spine, bending whichever way the wind blows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有脊梁的委员会，风往哪吹就往哪倒。

abstract.en: Picture a mayfly in a stream acting as a tiny water-quality meter.
abstract.cn: 想象溪流里一只蜉蝣，充当一枚微小的水质计。

examples.en: Invertebrates make up roughly ninety-five per cent of animal species.
examples.cn: 无脊椎动物约占动物物种的百分之九十五。

examples.en: The survey recorded invertebrates but no vertebrates in the polluted stream.
examples.cn: 调查在被污染的溪流中记录到无脊椎动物，却没有脊椎动物。

examples.en: The minister was called invertebrate for refusing to defend the policy.
examples.cn: 这位部长因拒绝为该政策辩护而被称为没有骨气。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（不）+ vertebrate（有脊椎的）——没有脊椎的动物；记「软体、虫、虾蟹都不靠脊梁」

root: 拉丁 in-「不」+ vertebra「脊椎骨节」（源自 vertere「转动」）+ -ate；vertebra 的更深词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one negative fact, the absence of a spine, through zoology, palaeontology, ecology, fisheries, metaphor and pollution monitoring.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕一个否定事实——没有脊柱，穿过动物学、古生物学、生态学、渔业、比喻与污染监测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft body in a tide pool, held up by water rather than bone.
core.cn: 核心意象：潮池里一具柔软的身体，靠水而非骨骼支撑。

branches.en: ABSENCE: noun and adjective both say the same thing, that there is no vertebral column.
branches.cn: 缺失：名词与形容词说的是同一件事——没有脊柱。

branches.en: A FIELD: because the category is so wide, it becomes a branch of zoology.
branches.cn: 一个学科：范畴太宽，于是成了一门动物学分支。

branches.en: HARD PARTS IN SOFT ANIMALS: shells and exoskeletons dominate the fossil and reef records.
branches.cn: 软体中的硬部件：贝壳与外骨骼主导了化石与礁体记录。

branches.en: RESOURCE AND INSTRUMENT: food from the sea, and a meter for its health.
branches.cn: 资源与仪器：既是海中食物，也是衡量其健康的仪表。

branches.en: METAPHOR: no spine becomes no courage.
branches.cn: 比喻：没有脊柱变成了没有骨气。

intro.en: Invertebrate is a prefixed derivative of vertebra, so its parts are a negative prefix, a noun and an adjective ending.
intro.cn: invertebrate 是 vertebra 的加缀派生词，其成分是否定前缀、名词与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertebra comes from vertere 'to turn'; in- negates it, and -atus supplies the adjective shape that English reduced to -ate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vertebra 来自 vertere「转动」；in- 加以否定，-atus 提供形容词形态，英语简化为 -ate。

items.example: The prefix denies the spine.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀否定了脊柱的存在。

items.example: Each vertebra turns slightly on the next.
items.exampleCN: 每块椎骨都能相对下一块略微转动。

items.example: The ending makes the word an adjective as well as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使该词兼作形容词与名词。

items.example: The invertebrate has no spinal column.
items.exampleCN: 这只无脊椎动物没有脊柱。

items.example: Invertebrates fill the stream bed.
items.exampleCN: 无脊椎动物布满溪床。

items.example: Vertebrates are the minority of animal species.
items.exampleCN: 脊椎动物只占动物物种的少数。

items.example: The vertebral column protects the nerve cord.
items.exampleCN: 脊柱保护着神经索。

items.example: Invert shares the turning root but not the meaning.
items.exampleCN: invert 同出「转」词根，但意义不同。

definition_en: an animal with a backbone, or having a backbone
core_image: 一条完整的脊柱从颅骨延伸到尾端，一节节椎骨串成不间断的链
scene: 解剖台上，一只小动物的脊柱被完整取出，一节节椎骨从颅骨一直串到尾端。 The vertebrate spine ran from skull to tail in one unbroken chain of bones.
sceneCN: 这里 vertebrate 指「脊椎动物的」（第 1 个义项：有脊柱的动物），在此作定语；句意为这只脊椎动物的脊柱从颅骨到尾端串成一条不间断的骨链。

senses.title: An animal with a backbone
senses.definition: any animal with a vertebral column, including fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals
senses.definitionCN: 任何有脊柱的动物，包括鱼、两栖动物、爬行动物、鸟类与哺乳动物
senses.example: The vertebrate spine ran from skull to tail in one chain.
senses.exampleCN: 这只脊椎动物的脊柱从颅骨到尾端串成一条链。
senses.why: The word is built directly on vertebra, the bones that make up the spine, so the backbone is the defining trait.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接建立在 vertebra（构成脊柱的骨节）之上，因此脊柱就是定义特征。

senses.title: The adjective: having a backbone
senses.definition: describing an animal or structure that possesses a spinal column
senses.definitionCN: 描述拥有脊柱的动物或结构
senses.example: The vertebrate body plan includes a skull and a closed circulatory system.
senses.exampleCN: 脊椎动物的身体结构包括颅骨与闭锁式循环系统。
senses.why: As with invertebrate, noun and adjective share one form, so the same word can modify another noun.
senses.whyCN: 与 invertebrate 一样，名词和形容词同形，因此同一个词可以修饰另一个名词。

senses.title: The group as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的脊椎动物类群
senses.definition: the vertebrates collectively, a subphylum of the chordates
senses.definitionCN: 所有脊椎动物的集合，是脊索动物门下的一个亚门
senses.example: Vertebrates are a small fraction of all animal species.
senses.exampleCN: 脊椎动物只占全部动物物种的一小部分。
senses.why: Although familiar, the group is numerically small, and the plural is used for the category rather than for a herd.
senses.whyCN: 这一类群虽为人熟悉，数量却很少，因此复数形式指的是范畴，而不是一群个体。

senses.title: The subject of vertebrate palaeontology
senses.titleCN: 脊椎动物古生物学的研究对象
senses.definition: fossil vertebrates, studied for evidence of evolution and past environments
senses.definitionCN: 化石脊椎动物，用于研究演化与古环境
senses.example: Vertebrate fossils in the badlands trace the rise of mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 荒地上的脊椎动物化石记录了哺乳动物的兴起。
senses.why: The field needs the adjective because it studies bones and teeth, which are vertebrate specialities.
senses.whyCN: 这一领域需要这个形容词，因为它研究骨骼与牙齿，而这是脊椎动物的特长。

senses.title: A laboratory model animal
senses.definition: a vertebrate used in research, such as a mouse or zebrafish
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究的脊椎动物，如小鼠或斑马鱼
senses.example: The mouse is the standard vertebrate model for genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 小鼠是遗传学的标准脊椎动物模型。
senses.why: Medical research contrasts vertebrate models with invertebrate ones, and the adjective marks that distinction.
senses.whyCN: 医学研究把脊椎动物模型与无脊椎动物模型相对照，这个形容词正标出这一区别。

senses.title: A surveyed vertebrate fauna
senses.titleCN: 调查所得的脊椎动物群
senses.definition: the vertebrate species recorded in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区记录到的脊椎动物物种
senses.example: The vertebrate fauna of the island includes no large predators.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的脊椎动物群中没有大型捕食者。
senses.why: Surveys separate vertebrate from invertebrate records because the methods and expertise differ.
senses.whyCN: 调查把脊椎动物与无脊椎动物记录分开，因为方法与专业不同。

senses.title: A vertebrate pest
senses.definition: a vertebrate that damages crops, property or ecosystems, such as a rodent
senses.definitionCN: 损害作物、财产或生态系统的脊椎动物，如啮齿类
senses.example: Rodent control targets vertebrate pests rather than insects.
senses.exampleCN: 鼠类防治针对的是脊椎动物有害生物，而不是昆虫。
senses.why: Pest management uses the category to separate rodent and bird problems from insect problems.
senses.whyCN: 有害生物管理用这一范畴把鼠类与鸟类问题同昆虫问题分开。

senses.title: A conservation unit
senses.definition: a vertebrate species or population managed for conservation
senses.definitionCN: 为保护而管理的脊椎动物物种或种群
senses.example: The park monitors vertebrate populations every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 公园每年春天监测脊椎动物种群。
senses.why: Conservation reporting often counts vertebrates because they are large, visible and easy to survey.
senses.whyCN: 保护报告常统计脊椎动物，因为它们体型大、可见、易于调查。

intro.en: Vertebrate is Latin vertebra 'spinal joint' plus the adjective ending -ate; zoology adopted it as a group name in the modern period. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vertebrate 由拉丁 vertebra「脊椎关节」加形容词词尾 -ate 构成；动物学在近代把它采用为类群名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertebra meant 'joint', especially a joint of the spine, from vertere 'to turn'. The connection with turning is generally accepted; the earlier root is reconstructed.
items.cn: vertebra 意为「关节」，尤指脊柱关节，来自 vertere「转动」。与「转动」的联系一般被接受；更早的词根属重构。

items.en: Vertebratus meant 'jointed, provided with vertebrae', an adjective formed from the noun, and it supplied the shape of the English word.
items.cn: vertebratus 意为「有关节的、具椎骨的」，是由名词构成的形容词，提供了英语词的形态。

items.en: Lamarck's classification used vertébrés for backboned animals in the early nineteenth century, pairing it with invertébrés.
items.cn: 拉马克在 19 世纪初的分类中用 vertébrés 指有脊柱的动物，与 invertébrés 相对。

items.en: English vertebrate appears in the nineteenth century as noun and adjective, first in zoological and anatomical writing.
items.cn: 英语 vertebrate 在 19 世纪出现，兼作名词与形容词，最初见于动物学与解剖学文字。

items.en: Vertebrate palaeontology became a distinct field as fossil bones and teeth were catalogued separately from shelled invertebrates.
items.cn: 随着化石骨骼与牙齿同带壳的无脊椎动物分开编目，脊椎动物古生物学成为独立领域。

items.en: Source uncertain (details only): the Latin stages are clear, but the pre-Latin root of vertere is reconstructed and the exact first English citation is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅细节）：拉丁阶段清楚，但 vertere 的拉丁语之前词根属重构，英语确切首见书证也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the vertebra family that are easily swapped; group two holds broader or neighbouring animal categories.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 vertebra 词族、容易混用的词；第二组是更宽或相邻的动物范畴。

entries.definition: An animal without a backbone; the only difference is the prefix in-, which reverses the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 没有脊柱的动物；唯一差别是否定前缀 in-，意义正好相反。

entries.definition: A single spinal bone; the animal word is built on it, but the bone is not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 单块脊椎骨；动物词由它构成，但骨不等于动物。

entries.definition: Relating to vertebrae or the spine, as in vertebral column; it does not name an animal group.
entries.definitionCN: 与椎骨或脊柱有关，如 vertebral column；它不指动物类群。

entries.definition: The formal Latin name of the group; Vertebrata is the whole subphylum, vertebrate is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 该群的正式拉丁名；Vertebrata 是整个亚门，vertebrate 是其中一个成员。

entries.definition: Any animal with a notochord at some stage, including vertebrates and some invertebrates; it is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 任何在某一阶段具脊索的动物，包括脊椎动物与部分无脊椎动物；范围更宽。

entries.definition: A vertebrate with four limbs, such as a mammal, bird or reptile; fish are vertebrates but not tetrapods.
entries.definitionCN: 有四肢的脊椎动物，如哺乳动物、鸟或爬行动物；鱼是脊椎动物但不是四足动物。

entries.definition: A warm-blooded vertebrate that feeds its young milk; mammals are one class within Vertebrata.
entries.definitionCN: 以乳汁哺育幼崽的温血脊椎动物；哺乳动物是脊椎动物亚门中的一个纲。

entries.definition: An animal with a skull, essentially synonymous with vertebrate in modern usage but defined by the head shield.
entries.definitionCN: 有颅骨的动物，现代用法中基本与脊椎动物同义，但定义依据是头骨。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Vertebra is the bone; vertebrate is the animal that has a chain of them.
normal.cn: vertebra 是骨头；vertebrate 是拥有这一串骨头的动物。

normal.en: Fish, frogs, snakes, birds and mice are all vertebrates; insects and crabs are not.
normal.cn: 鱼、蛙、蛇、鸟、鼠都是脊椎动物；昆虫与蟹不是。

normal.en: The negative prefix in- turns vertebrate into its opposite, invertebrate.
normal.cn: 否定前缀 in- 把 vertebrate 变成反义词 invertebrate。

normal.en: Vertebrate palaeontology studies bones and teeth; invertebrate palaeontology studies shells.
normal.cn: 脊椎动物古生物学研究骨骼与牙齿；无脊椎动物古生物学研究贝壳。

normal.en: Vertebrata is the subphylum; vertebrate is one member.
normal.cn: Vertebrata 是亚门；vertebrate 是一个成员。

abstract.en: Picture a rope of bone running from head to tail, holding the whole body together.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从头顶贯到尾端的骨绳，把整个身体串起来。

abstract.en: Picture a museum hall where teeth and bones tell a story shells cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一座博物馆大厅，牙齿与骨骼讲述着贝壳讲不出的故事。

abstract.en: Picture a mouse in a lab standing in for the whole vertebrate line.
abstract.cn: 想象实验室里一只小鼠，代表整条脊椎动物演化线。

examples.en: Only about five per cent of described animal species are vertebrates.
examples.cn: 已描述的动物物种中只有约百分之五为脊椎动物。

examples.en: The vertebrate fossil record begins in the Cambrian seas.
examples.cn: 脊椎动物的化石记录始于寒武纪海洋。

examples.en: Vertebrate pests such as rats damage both crops and stored grain.
examples.cn: 鼠类等脊椎动物有害生物既损害作物也损害仓储谷物。

dict_mnemonic.text: vertebra（椎骨）+ ate——身上有一串椎骨的动物，就是脊椎动物；记「有脊梁的才算」

root: 拉丁 vertebra「脊椎关节」（源自 vertere「转动」）+ -ate；vertebra 的更深词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one backbone through zoology, palaeontology, laboratory work, field surveys, pest control and conservation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一条脊柱穿过动物学、古生物学、实验室工作、野外调查、有害生物防治与保护工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain of vertebrae running from skull to tail without a break.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串椎骨从颅骨连到尾端，中间没有断开。

branches.en: THE SPINE: noun and adjective both rest on the presence of vertebrae.
branches.cn: 脊柱：名词与形容词都建立在「有椎骨」这一点上。

branches.en: A SMALL, FAMILIAR GROUP: numerous as individuals, few as species.
branches.cn: 小而熟悉的类群：个体多，物种少。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: bones and teeth carry the vertebrate fossil record.
branches.cn: 深时：骨骼与牙齿承载着脊椎动物的化石记录。

branches.en: EXPERIMENT: a mouse or fish stands in for the whole subphylum.
branches.cn: 实验：一只小鼠或一条鱼代表整个亚门。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: survey it, control it, or protect it.
branches.cn: 管理：调查它、防治它，或保护它。

intro.en: Vertebrate is a noun-derived adjective in -ate, with a negative twin in in- and a formal group name in Vertebrata.
intro.cn: vertebrate 是由名词派生的 -ate 形容词，有 in- 构成的否定孪生词，也有正式类群名 Vertebrata。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertebra 'joint' comes from vertere 'to turn'; vertebratus is the adjective, and Vertebrata is the modern group name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vertebra「关节」来自 vertere「转动」；vertebratus 是形容词，Vertebrata 是近代类群名。

items.example: Each vertebra is a separate bone.
items.exampleCN: 每块椎骨都是独立的骨。

items.example: The ending turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成形容词。

items.example: A vertebrate has a spinal column.
items.exampleCN: 脊椎动物有脊柱。

items.example: Vertebrates are outnumbered by invertebrates.
items.exampleCN: 脊椎动物在数量上不及无脊椎动物。

items.example: The prefix reverses the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀反转词义。

items.example: An invertebrate has no spine.
items.exampleCN: 无脊椎动物没有脊柱。

items.example: Vertebrata belongs within the chordates.
items.exampleCN: 脊椎动物亚门属于脊索动物。

items.example: The vertebral column is the backbone.
items.exampleCN: 脊柱就是那条脊梁。

definition_zh: 两栖动物；两栖的；水陆两用飞行器
definition_en: an animal that lives both in water and on land, especially a frog, toad or salamander, or a vehicle that moves on both water and land
core_image: 一只蛙蹲在岸边，一半身体泡在浅水里，一半趴在湿泥上
scene: 池塘边，一只蛙半身泡在浅水里，半身趴在湿泥上，随时准备跳回水中。 The amphibian rested with its hind legs in the water and its head on the mud.
sceneCN: 这里 amphibian 指「两栖动物」（第 1 个义项：既能在水中又能在陆上生活的动物）；句意为这只两栖动物后腿泡在水里、头搁在泥上休息。

senses.title: An animal of the class Amphibia
senses.definition: a vertebrate that usually begins life in water and later lives on land, such as a frog, toad or salamander
senses.definitionCN: 通常在水中开始生命、之后在陆地生活的脊椎动物，如蛙、蟾蜍或蝾螈
senses.example: The amphibian rested with its hind legs in the water.
senses.exampleCN: 这只两栖动物后腿泡在水里休息。
senses.why: The Greek name means 'living both ways', and the animal's life cycle really does divide between water and land.
senses.whyCN: 希腊原名意为「两种生活」，而这种动物的生活史确实在水与陆之间分成两段。

senses.title: The group as a whole
senses.definition: the amphibians collectively, treated as one vertebrate class
senses.definitionCN: 所有两栖动物的集合，作为一个脊椎动物纲
senses.example: Amphibians are the most threatened vertebrate class.
senses.exampleCN: 两栖动物是受威胁最严重的脊椎动物纲。
senses.why: Because the group is a formal class, the plural often names the category rather than a pond full of frogs.
senses.whyCN: 由于这一类群是正式的一个纲，复数常指范畴，而不是一池塘的蛙。

senses.title: The adjective: amphibious
senses.definition: describing an animal or vehicle able to operate both in water and on land
senses.definitionCN: 描述能在水中与陆上两处活动的动物或交通工具
senses.example: The amphibian truck crossed the river without a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆水陆两用车没有桥也过了河。
senses.why: The adjective widens 'two lives' from biology to machinery, since a vehicle can also live in two elements.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把「两种生活」从生物学扩展到机械，因为车辆也能在两个介质中活动。

senses.title: Amphibian decline and conservation
senses.definition: the documented worldwide loss of amphibian populations and the efforts to slow it
senses.definitionCN: 有记录的全球两栖动物种群减少，以及减缓这一趋势的努力
senses.example: Amphibian decline is linked to habitat loss and fungal disease.
senses.exampleCN: 两栖动物衰退与栖息地丧失及真菌疾病有关。
senses.why: Conservation writing needed a short label for a global pattern, and the class name supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 保护文献需要一个简短标签来指一种全球现象，类群名正好提供。

senses.title: An amphibian as a bioindicator
senses.titleCN: 作为生物指示物的两栖动物
senses.definition: an amphibian used to judge environmental health because its skin is permeable and its life cycle exposes it to both water and land
senses.definitionCN: 因皮肤可渗透、生活史同时暴露于水陆而被用来判断环境健康的两栖动物
senses.example: Biologists count amphibians because they react quickly to pollution.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家统计两栖动物，因为它们对污染反应迅速。
senses.why: Their two-part life cycle makes them sensitive to changes in both habitats, which is exactly what a bioindicator needs.
senses.whyCN: 两段式生活史使它们对两种生境的变化都敏感，这正是生物指示物所需。

senses.title: An amphibian fossil
senses.definition: the preserved remains of an ancient amphibian, important for the move from water to land
senses.definitionCN: 古代两栖动物的遗骸，对研究从水到陆的转变很重要
senses.example: The amphibian fossil shows four limbs and a tail fin.
senses.exampleCN: 这块两栖动物化石显示出四肢与尾鳍。
senses.why: Early amphibians record the vertebrate invasion of land, so palaeontology uses the class name for a key transition.
senses.whyCN: 早期两栖动物记录了脊椎动物登陆，因此古生物学用这个纲名来指一次关键转变。

senses.title: A vehicle that travels on land and water
senses.definition: an aircraft or vehicle designed to operate from both land and water
senses.definitionCN: 设计为可在陆地与水面两处运行或起降的飞行器或车辆
senses.example: The old amphibian landed on the lake and taxied to the dock.
senses.exampleCN: 这架老式水陆两用飞机降落在湖面，滑行到码头。
senses.why: Aviation borrowed the biological word because the machine, like the frog, belongs to two elements.
senses.whyCN: 航空借用了生物学词，因为这种机器像蛙一样同属两个介质。

senses.title: The breeding pond habitat
senses.definition: the freshwater pond or wetland where amphibians gather to breed and lay eggs
senses.definitionCN: 两栖动物聚集繁殖、产卵的淡水池塘或湿地
senses.example: The farm's amphibian pond was full of egg clusters in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 春天农场的两栖动物池塘里满是卵块。
senses.why: Habitat studies name the pond by its users, so amphibian becomes an attributive label for a specific kind of wetland.
senses.whyCN: 栖息地研究以使用者来命名池塘，因此 amphibian 成了某类湿地的定语标签。

intro.en: Amphibian is Greek amphibios 'living both ways', built from amphi- 'both' and bios 'life', borrowed through Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: amphibian 是希腊 amphibios「两种生活」，由 amphi-「两者」与 bios「生命」构成，经拉丁语借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Amphi- meant 'both, on both sides', the same prefix heard in amphitheatre and amphora.
items.cn: amphi- 意为「两者、两侧」，同一前缀也见于 amphitheatre 与 amphora。

items.en: Bios meant 'life, mode of life'; it is the source of biology and biography, and of the -bios in symbiotic.
items.cn: bios 意为「生命、生活方式」；biology 与 biography 都源自它，symbiotic 中的 -bios 也来自它。

items.en: Amphibios described animals that live both in water and on land; Greek naturalists used it for frogs and similar creatures.
items.cn: amphibios 描述既在水中又在陆上生活的动物；希腊博物学家用它指蛙及类似生物。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as amphibius, and English took the noun through learned Latin in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊形容词为 amphibius；英语在 17 世纪经学术拉丁语引入该名词。

items.en: Eighteenth-century zoology fixed Amphibia as a class, and amphibian became the everyday noun for its members.
items.cn: 18 世纪动物学把 Amphibia 固定为一个纲，amphibian 成为其成员的日常名词。

items.en: Source uncertain (details only): the Greek compound is clear, but the exact first English use is approximate, and the older claim that the word literally meant 'two lives' is a modern gloss rather than a Greek definition.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅细节）：希腊复合词清楚，但英语确切首见年代只是约数；旧说该词字面即「两条命」，那是现代解释，而非希腊语原定义。

note.en: Group one holds forms and derivatives of the same word; group two holds animal groups and terms that are often confused with amphibians.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的形式与派生词；第二组是常与两栖动物混淆的动物类群与术语。

entries.definition: The Latin-shaped adjective meaning 'two-element'; amphibian can also be an adjective, but amphibious is the usual one for vehicles and operations.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁形态的形容词，意为「两介质的」；amphibian 也可作形容词，但车辆与行动更常用 amphibious。

entries.definition: The formal Latin class name; Amphibia is the whole class, an amphibian is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 正式拉丁纲名；Amphibia 是整个纲，amphibian 是一个成员。

entries.definition: A group of rock-forming minerals, from a different Greek word about ambiguity; the resemblance to amphibian is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 一类造岩矿物，来自另一个表示「歧义」的希腊词；与 amphibian 的相似属偶然。

entries.definition: The study of amphibians, built with -logy; it names a field, not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 研究两栖动物的学科，由 -logy 构成；它指领域，不指动物。

entries.definition: A scaly, air-breathing vertebrate that usually lays shelled eggs on land; reptiles are not amphibians, though the groups are often paired.
entries.definitionCN: 有鳞、用肺呼吸、通常在陆地产硬壳卵的脊椎动物；爬行动物不是两栖动物，尽管两类常被并提。

entries.definition: The water-living larva of a frog or toad; it is one stage of an amphibian, not the class.
entries.definitionCN: 蛙或蟾蜍的水生幼体；它是两栖动物的一个阶段，不是整个纲。

entries.definition: A tailed amphibian with four legs; it is a member of the class, not a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 有尾、有四足的两栖动物；它是纲内成员，不是纲的同义词。

entries.definition: Living in water; an amphibian is only partly aquatic, since it also depends on land or damp air.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在水中；两栖动物只部分水生，因为它也依赖陆地或潮湿空气。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: amphi- 'both' + bios 'life': the animal with two lives, one in water and one on land.
normal.cn: amphi-「两者」+ bios「生命」：过着两种生活的动物，一种在水里，一种在陆上。

normal.en: Frogs, toads and salamanders are amphibians; turtles and snakes are reptiles.
normal.cn: 蛙、蟾蜍、蝾螈是两栖动物；龟与蛇是爬行动物。

normal.en: A tadpole is a larval amphibian, not a separate kind of animal.
normal.cn: 蝌蚪是两栖动物的幼体，不是另一类动物。

normal.en: Amphibious is the usual adjective for vehicles; amphibian is the usual noun for the animal.
normal.cn: 车辆通常用 amphibious 作形容词；动物通常用 amphibian 作名词。

normal.en: Amphibian decline is the fixed phrase for the global loss of these populations.
normal.cn: amphibian decline 是描述全球两栖动物种群衰退的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a body half in water and half in air, belonging fully to neither.
abstract.cn: 想象一具半在水里、半在空气中的身体，哪一边都不完全属于。

abstract.en: Picture a frog as a warning light for the health of a whole wetland.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蛙是一整片湿地健康的警示灯。

abstract.en: Picture a truck that keeps driving straight into a river.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆卡车径直开进河里还继续走。

examples.en: Amphibians usually return to water to breed.
examples.cn: 两栖动物通常回到水中繁殖。

examples.en: The amphibian's permeable skin makes it sensitive to drought.
examples.cn: 两栖动物可渗透的皮肤使它对干旱很敏感。

examples.en: An amphibian aircraft can use a lake as a runway.
examples.cn: 水陆两用飞机可以把湖面当跑道。

dict_mnemonic.text: amphi（两边）+ bian（生命）——两边都能活的动物，就是两栖动物；记「水里一半、岸上一半」

root: 希腊 amphi-「两者」+ bios「生命」→ amphibios「两种生活」→ 拉丁 amphibius；希腊复合义清楚，英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a two-element animal from pond to class to crisis: the animal, the group, the adjective, the decline, the bioindicator, the fossil, the amphibious vehicle and the breeding pond.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一种双介质动物从池塘走到纲、再走到危机：动物、类群、形容词、种群衰退、生物指示、化石、水陆两用车与繁殖池塘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frog at the water's edge, half in and half out.
core.cn: 核心意象：水边的一只蛙，一半在水里，一半在外。

branches.en: ANIMAL AND CLASS: one frog, or the whole vertebrate class.
branches.cn: 动物与纲：一只蛙，或整个脊椎动物纲。

branches.en: TWO ELEMENTS: the same logic extends from an animal to a machine.
branches.cn: 两个介质：同一逻辑从动物扩展到机器。

branches.en: WARNING: what makes them sensitive makes them threatened and useful as indicators.
branches.cn: 警示：使它们敏感的特性，既让它们受威胁，也让它们成为有用的指示物。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: early amphibians record the move onto land.
branches.cn: 深时：早期两栖动物记录了登陆的过程。

branches.en: PLACE: the breeding pond is named after the animals that use it.
branches.cn: 地点：繁殖池塘以使用它的动物来命名。

intro.en: Amphibian is a Greek compound seen through Latin, so its parts are two Greek roots plus an English noun ending.
intro.cn: amphibian 是经拉丁语转手的希腊复合词，其成分是两个希腊词根加一个英语名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek amphi- and bios formed amphibios; Latin borrowed it as amphibius, and English added the noun ending -ian.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 amphi- 与 bios 构成 amphibios；拉丁借作 amphibius，英语再加上名词词尾 -ian。

items.example: The prefix supplies the idea of doubleness.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供「双重」的意思。

items.example: The second element supplies the idea of living.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供「活着」的意思。

items.meaning: an animal living in two elements
items.meaningCN: 在两种介质中生活的动物
items.example: The amphibian laid its eggs in the pond.
items.exampleCN: 这只两栖动物把卵产在池塘里。

items.example: Amphibians need damp cover.
items.exampleCN: 两栖动物需要潮湿的遮蔽。

items.meaning: able to operate on land and water
items.example: The amphibious force landed at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 两栖部队在黎明登陆。

items.example: The suffix makes a noun of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表归属的名词。

items.example: Amphibia is a class of vertebrates.
items.exampleCN: 两栖纲是脊椎动物的一纲。

items.example: Amphibiology grew alongside ecology.
items.exampleCN: 两栖动物学与生态学一同发展。

latinEntries.meaning: living both in water and on land

definition_zh: 爬行动物；爬虫；（贬义）卑劣的人
definition_en: a cold-blooded vertebrate with scales that lays eggs on land, such as a snake, lizard or turtle, or a contemptible person
core_image: 一只蜥蜴腹部几乎贴地，四肢向两侧撑开，在热石上缓缓前行
scene: 沙漠的岩石上，一只蜥蜴腹部贴地，四肢向两侧撑开，慢慢向前爬。 The reptile moved low over the hot stone, its belly almost touching the surface.
sceneCN: 这里 reptile 指「爬行动物」（第 1 个义项：体表有鳞、在陆上产卵的变温脊椎动物）；句意为这只爬行动物贴着滚烫的石头低身前行，腹部几乎碰到地面。

derivatives.zh: 爬行动物的；像爬行动物的

senses.title: A scaly, cold-blooded vertebrate
senses.titleCN: 体表有鳞的变温脊椎动物
senses.definition: a vertebrate with dry scaly skin that regulates its body temperature by behaviour and usually lays eggs on land
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤干燥有鳞、靠行为调节体温、通常在陆上产卵的脊椎动物
senses.example: The reptile moved low over the hot stone.
senses.exampleCN: 这只爬行动物贴着热石低身前行。
senses.why: The Latin name means 'creeping thing', and the defining traits are scales and a body that must warm itself in the sun.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁原名意为「爬行的东西」，其标志特征是鳞片与必须靠晒太阳取暖的身体。

senses.title: The class Reptilia as a whole
senses.definition: the reptiles collectively, a vertebrate class that in modern classification includes birds
senses.definitionCN: 所有爬行动物的集合，现代分类中这一纲还包括鸟类
senses.example: Reptiles occupy every continent except Antarctica.
senses.exampleCN: 除南极洲外，每个大陆都有爬行动物。
senses.why: Because the class is a formal unit, the plural often names a category rather than individual animals.
senses.whyCN: 因为这是一个正式分类单元，复数常指范畴而不是个体动物。

senses.title: A reptile kept as a pet
senses.titleCN: 作为宠物饲养的爬行动物
senses.definition: a snake, lizard or turtle kept in a terrarium and sold through the pet trade
senses.definitionCN: 养在饲养箱中、经宠物贸易出售的蛇、蜥蜴或龟
senses.example: The shop sells reptile supplies as well as the animals.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店既卖爬行动物，也卖饲养用品。
senses.why: The pet trade uses the class name as a market category, so reptile becomes a product label.
senses.whyCN: 宠物贸易把纲名当作市场类别，于是 reptile 成了产品标签。

senses.title: A venomous reptile
senses.definition: a reptile that injects venom through fangs or a sting, such as a viper
senses.definitionCN: 通过毒牙或毒刺注入毒液的爬行动物，如蝰蛇
senses.example: Antivenom is made from the venom of a reptile.
senses.exampleCN: 抗蛇毒血清由某种爬行动物的毒液制成。
senses.why: Medical writing uses the class name because the bite may come from a snake, a lizard or a turtle.
senses.whyCN: 医学文献用纲名，因为咬伤可能来自蛇、蜥蜴或龟。

senses.title: A fossil reptile
senses.definition: ancient reptile remains, including dinosaurs in traditional usage
senses.definitionCN: 古代爬行动物遗骸，传统用法中也包括恐龙
senses.example: The fossil reptile had a sail-like crest on its back.
senses.exampleCN: 这只爬行动物化石背部有帆状脊冠。
senses.why: Palaeontology long treated dinosaurs as reptiles, and the word still carries that history even though birds are their descendants.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学长期把恐龙当作爬行动物，这个词仍带着这段历史，尽管鸟类是恐龙的后代。

senses.title: The reptile house in a zoo
senses.definition: a heated building where snakes and other reptiles are displayed to the public
senses.definitionCN: 向公众展示蛇类等爬行动物、保持加热的馆舍
senses.example: The children queued for the reptile house.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们排队等着进爬行动物馆。
senses.why: Zoos needed a short exhibit label, and the class name became a building name.
senses.whyCN: 动物园需要简短的展区名称，纲名于是成了建筑名。

senses.title: A contemptible person
senses.definition: an insulting term for someone seen as low, treacherous or grovelling
senses.definitionCN: 蔑称，指低劣、阴险或谄媚的人
senses.example: The old pamphlet called the informer a reptile.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧小册子把告密者称为卑劣之徒。
senses.why: The insult draws on the animal's belly-down movement and its reputation for coldness, turning 'creeping' into moral contempt.
senses.whyCN: 这个骂法利用了动物贴地爬行的姿态与「冷血」的名声，把「爬」转成道德上的轻蔑。

senses.title: Reptile leather
senses.definition: the skin of a snake, crocodile or other reptile used for bags, belts and shoes
senses.definitionCN: 用于包、带、鞋的蛇、鳄等爬行动物皮革
senses.example: The belt was made of reptile skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这条腰带是爬行动物皮革做的。
senses.why: The material trade names the product by its source class, so reptile also functions as an attributive noun.
senses.whyCN: 材料行业按来源类群给产品命名，因此 reptile 也作定语名词使用。

intro.en: Reptile goes back to Latin repere 'to creep' through the adjective reptilis; the name describes how the animal moves, not how it is built. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: reptile 经形容词 reptilis 上溯到拉丁 repere「爬行」；这个名字描述的是行动方式，而非身体构造。年代均为约数。

items.en: Repere meant 'to creep, crawl'. Its deeper origin is not settled, so any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: repere 意为「爬行、匍匐」。其更深来源没有定论，凡为它提出的印欧词根都属重构。

items.en: Reptilis meant 'creeping, crawling', an adjective formed from the verb and used of animals that move close to the ground.
items.cn: reptilis 意为「爬行的、匍匐的」，由动词构成的形容词，用于贴地移动的动物。

items.en: English reptile is recorded from the late fourteenth century, first for creeping animals in general and later for the scaly vertebrate class.
items.cn: 英语 reptile 自 14 世纪后期有记录，最初泛指爬行动物，后来才专指有鳞的脊椎动物纲。

items.en: Eighteenth-century zoology fixed Reptilia as a class, separating snakes, lizards and turtles from amphibians and insects.
items.cn: 18 世纪动物学把 Reptilia 固定为一个纲，把蛇、蜥蜴、龟与两栖动物及昆虫分开。

items.en: From the eighteenth century 'reptile' was used as an insult for a low or grovelling person, drawing on the belly-down image.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，reptile 被用作侮辱语，指低劣或谄媚的人，取「贴地爬行」的形象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Latin stages are clear, but the pre-Latin origin of repere is unsettled and the exact first English citation is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：拉丁阶段清楚，但 repere 的拉丁语之前来源没有定论，英语确切首见书证也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same reptile stock; group two holds animal names and adjectives that are often misplaced around reptiles.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 reptile 词族的形式；第二组是常被误置于爬行动物语境中的动物名与形容词。

entries.definition: Of or like reptiles; as a noun in science fiction it also means a reptile-like being.
entries.definitionCN: 爬行动物的或像爬行动物的；在科幻作品中作名词还指似爬行类的人形生物。

entries.definition: The formal Latin class name; Reptilia is the whole class, a reptile is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 正式拉丁纲名；Reptilia 是整个纲，reptile 是一个成员。

entries.definition: A botanical adjective meaning creeping along the ground; it shares the Latin verb but describes plants.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学形容词，意为贴地匍匐；它同出拉丁动词，却描述植物。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'like', it describes a reptile-like form without claiming it belongs to the class.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -oid「像」构成，描述似爬行动物的形态，并不表示它属于该纲。

entries.definition: A vertebrate that usually breeds in water and has moist skin; it is not a reptile, though both are cold-blooded.
entries.definitionCN: 通常在水中繁殖、皮肤潮湿的脊椎动物；它不是爬行动物，尽管两者都是变温动物。

entries.definition: A small reptile with four legs and a long tail; it is one kind of reptile, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 有四足和长尾的小型爬行动物；它是爬行动物的一种，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A limbless reptile; again a member of the class rather than a general term.
entries.definitionCN: 无肢的爬行动物；同样是纲内成员，而不是泛称。

entries.definition: An animal that relies on external heat; reptiles are ectotherms, but so are many fish and invertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖外部热量的动物；爬行动物是变温动物，但许多鱼与无脊椎动物也是。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Reptile comes from 'to creep': the animal that moves with its belly near the ground.
normal.cn: reptile 来自「爬行」：腹部贴近地面移动的动物。

normal.en: Snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles are reptiles; frogs are amphibians.
normal.cn: 蛇、蜥蜴、龟、鳄是爬行动物；蛙是两栖动物。

normal.en: Reptilia is the class; reptile is one member; reptilian is the adjective.
normal.cn: Reptilia 是纲；reptile 是成员；reptilian 是形容词。

normal.en: Reptile house is the fixed zoo label for the heated exhibit building.
normal.cn: reptile house 是动物园里指加热展馆的固定说法。

normal.en: The insult 'reptile' plays on the same belly-down image, not on the biology.
normal.cn: 骂人的 reptile 用的是同一个「贴地」形象，与生物学无关。

abstract.en: Picture a body that must borrow its warmth from a stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一具必须向石头借温暖的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a creature that hears the ground through its jaw.
abstract.cn: 想象一个通过下颌听见大地的生物。

abstract.en: Picture an insult that crawls: the same word for an animal and for a person you despise.
abstract.cn: 想象一句会爬的骂人话：同一个词既指动物，也指你鄙视的人。

examples.en: Reptiles regulate their temperature by moving between sun and shade.
examples.cn: 爬行动物通过在阳光与阴影间移动来调节体温。

examples.en: The reptile house keeps the snakes warm through the winter.
examples.cn: 爬行动物馆让蛇整个冬天都保持温暖。

examples.en: The treaty restricts trade in reptile skins.
examples.cn: 该条约限制爬行动物皮革贸易。

dict_mnemonic.text: reptile 读起来像「瑞普泰尔」——贴地爬（rept-）的动物；记「肚皮贴地的都是爬行动物」

root: 拉丁 repere「爬行」→ reptilis「爬行的」→ 英语 reptile；repere 的更深词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a creeping animal from the desert floor to the pet shop, the antivenom lab, the fossil bed, the zoo building, the leather trade and finally to an insult for a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一种爬行动物从沙漠地面走到宠物店、抗毒血清实验室、化石层、动物园展馆、皮革贸易，最后变成对人的骂语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lizard moving belly-down across hot stone, legs splayed to the sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只蜥蜴腹部贴地、四肢向两侧张开，在热石上移动。

branches.en: ANIMAL AND CLASS: one creeping vertebrate, or the whole scaly class.
branches.cn: 动物与纲：一只爬行的脊椎动物，或整个有鳞的纲。

branches.en: HUMAN USE: a terrarium pet and a medical hazard.
branches.cn: 人的利用：既是被饲养的宠物，也是医学上的危险。

branches.en: MATERIAL TRACES: fossil bones and traded skins both carry the class name.
branches.cn: 物质痕迹：化石骨骼与交易皮革都带着纲名。

branches.en: DISPLAY: the heated zoo building is named after its inhabitants.
branches.cn: 展示：加热的动物园建筑以住户命名。

branches.en: THE INSULT: belly-down movement becomes moral lowliness.
branches.cn: 骂语：贴地而行变成了道德上的低劣。

intro.en: Reptile is a Latin verb turned adjective turned English noun; the stem also gives reptilian and the class name Reptilia.
intro.cn: reptile 是拉丁动词变形容词、再变英语名词的结果；同一词干还给出 reptilian 与纲名 Reptilia。

latinIntro.en: Latin repere 'to creep' yields reptilis and reptilium; English draws reptile, reptilian and reptant from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 repere「爬行」衍生 reptilis 与 reptilium；英语的 reptile、reptilian、reptant 都取自这一词族。

items.example: The stem supplies the crawling image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供「爬行」的形象。

items.example: Reptilis means able to creep.
items.exampleCN: reptilis 意为会爬行的。

items.example: The reptile basked on the rock.
items.exampleCN: 这只爬行动物在岩石上晒太阳。

items.example: Reptiles need warmth to digest food.
items.exampleCN: 爬行动物需要温暖才能消化食物。

items.example: Reptilian means belonging to the reptiles.
items.exampleCN: reptilian 意为属于爬行动物的。

items.meaningCN: 爬行动物的；像爬行动物的
items.example: The reptilian eye never blinks.
items.exampleCN: 那只爬行动物般的眼睛从不眨。

items.meaning: creeping, as of a plant stem
items.example: The reptant stem rooted at each node.
items.exampleCN: 匍匐茎在每个节处生根。

items.example: Reptilia includes snakes and turtles.
items.exampleCN: 爬行纲包括蛇与龟。

definition_zh: 爬行动物的；像爬行动物的；冷酷阴险的
definition_en: relating to or resembling reptiles, or cold and unemotional like a reptile
core_image: 特写中一只蜥蜴的竖瞳在冷光下缩成细缝，毫无表情
scene: 特写镜头里，蜥蜴的竖瞳在冷光中缩成一条细缝，一动不动。 The reptilian eye narrowed to a vertical slit in the cold light.
sceneCN: 这里 reptilian 指「爬行动物般的」（第 1 个义项：属于或类似爬行动物的）；句意为那只爬行动物般的眼睛在冷光中缩成一条竖缝。

爬行类生物；似爬行类的人形生物（科幻用法）

collocations.zh: 爬行动物脑（原始本能层面的比喻）
